a14.speaker: Ahmed Assid, Amazigh rights activist
a14.speech: Points out the slow disappearance of the Tamazight language, even though it is considered the living heart of Amazigh identity.

a363.speaker: Reverend Charles Chelenshya, Kitwe-based clergyman
a363.speech: Appealed to the government to expedite the Konkola Copper Mine (KCM) transition process by ensuring that the scheme of arrangement is concluded this month; said that now that drought had been declared a national disaster, and resources were needed to address the situation, it was important that the mining sector was fully revamped.

a508.speaker: Moeti Mohwasa, Minister for State Presidency (Botswana)
a508.speech: Did not answer a question about alleged corruption at Botswana Television because the Speaker of Parliament deemed the answer too long, and instead submitted a written reply.

a508.speaker: Speaker of Parliament (Botswana)
a508.speech: Deemed the answer too long, and so the minister instead submitted a written reply.

a508.speaker: Leepetswe Lesedi, Member of Parliament for Serowe West
a508.speech: Had asked the question about alleged corruption at Botswana Television.

a508.speaker: Moeti Mohwasa, Minister for State Presidency (Botswana)
a508.speech: In his written response, revealed that Dignity Investment (Pty) Ltd was granted a single direct appointment in 2018, amounting to P296 800, for assessing the Mass Media Electrical System following persistent electrical instability at the complex; that Mag and Beauty Studio, since its inception, received four open public tenders totalling approximately P14.2 million, that the company has not been engaged by DBS since 2021 and that BTV presenters now rely on qualified freelancers for make-up services; that, contrary to some reports, Focused Engineering Solution (FES) was never awarded a tender for the relocation of generators but instead submitted an assessment report in May 2018 proposing a P17 million solution, which was never implemented due to budgetary constraints; that several citizen-owned companies were engaged on an emergency basis for electrical maintenance, including TNS Maintenance Pty Ltd for P700 000, Electroflex Pty Ltd at P900 000 and Dongati Holdings Pty Ltd at P55 000; that Telemedia, 5AM Holdings and Aerocom were awarded tenders for the supply and training of three Fly Away Kits each valued at about P1.2 million; that the transport vehicle for Botswana Television was procured through the Central Transport Organisation for P550 000 with modifications costing an additional P18 000; that DBS saw four contract extensions between May 2011 and November 2021, all attributed to ongoing public tender evaluations; and that all three qualifying bidding companies were given equal opportunities for oral presentations and demonstrations in the same studio. These developments highlight the department's approach to procurement, emergency responses, and the management of public resources in maintaining and upgrading broadcasting facilities, Mohwasa said.

a631.speaker: National Building Society (NBS)
a631.speech: Says the long outstanding Dzivarasekwa housing project will be completed next month, while the Tynwald cluster development is set to be completed by December this year.

a661.speaker: Dr Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, interim resident representative of the World Health Organization (WHO) in Benin
a661.speech: Noted that in Benin malaria is an endemic disease with seasonal upsurges, particularly in May-June and September-October; that all age groups are affected but pregnant women and children under five are the most vulnerable and exposed to severe forms; and that malaria accounts for 44.9% of medical consultations in Benin, with a mortality rate of one death per 1,000 malaria cases.

a661.speaker: Dr Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, interim resident representative of the World Health Organization (WHO) in Benin
a661.speech: Acknowledged that Benin has chosen to invest massively in the fight against malaria and to work towards its development, giving itself the means to significantly reduce maternal and infant mortality, and that the launch of household enumeration and coupon distribution is a fundamental step in the free distribution of long-lasting insecticidal nets for 2020 ; urged every household to be enumerated in order to obtain its insecticide-treated net on distribution day.

a661.speaker: Carl Anderson, USAID representative in Benin
a661.speech: Expressed his support for the campaign, which constitutes an excellent opportunity to pay particular attention to the burden of malaria - a strategy supported by USAID that is part of the government's Action Programme, aimed at contributing to the reduction of malaria-related morbidity and mortality.

a661.speaker: Benjamin Hounkpatin, Minister of Health of Benin
a661.speech: Said Benin has improved its coverage of long-lasting insecticidal nets through routine distribution and the campaigns organised in 2007, 2011, 2014 and 2017, the last of which aimed to restore universal access to LLINs and improve their use ; said that, drawing lessons from the 2017 campaign and taking account of information and communication technologies, a digitalisation approach has been adopted for the 2020 edition, using electronic collection of enumeration data and bar codes to confirm coupons and hand over nets, which saves time, ensures households actually received the nets, and provides daily instant results for each locality and verification of the quality of the enumeration.

a661.speaker: Benjamin Hounkpatin, Minister of Health of Benin
a661.speech: Recalled the results of the 2017 Demographic and Health Survey, which showed that ownership of long-lasting insecticidal nets rose remarkably from 25% in 2006 to 92% in 2017, and that use of LLINs also increased among children under five (from 20.1% to 82%) and among pregnant women (from 19.6% to 85%).

a661.speaker: 2017 Demographic and Health Survey (Benin)
a661.speech: Showed that ownership of long-lasting insecticidal nets progressed from 25% to 92% between 2006 and 2017, and that use increased among children under five (20.1% to 82%) and pregnant women (19.6% to 85%).

a708.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO) leadership
a708.speech: Bemoaned the decision by the United States to withdraw from WHO; the organisation noted that US funding provides the backbone for many of its large-scale emergency operations aimed at combating diseases globally, and stated: "US funding covers 95 per cent of the WHO's tuberculosis programme in Europe, along with 60 per cent of the agency's TB efforts in Africa, the Western Pacific, and headquarters in Geneva."

a708.speaker: WHO financing data
a708.speech: According to financing data, the US contributed an estimated $988 million between January and November 2024, marking approximately 14 per cent of WHO's $6.9 billion budget.

a708.speaker: African Union (AU) Commission (statement)
a708.speech: Expressed deep concern over the US withdrawal from WHO; in a statement the Commission emphasised the crucial role the US has played in shaping global health standards over the past seven decades, and noted that the US was a key supporter in establishing the Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), which works closely with WHO to tackle global health challenges.

a708.speaker: Dambisa Moyo, Zambian economist, author of 'Dead Aid: Why Aid Is Not Working and How There Is a Better Way for Africa' (2009)
a708.speech: Argues that foreign aid has failed to lift Africa out of poverty and has instead created a culture of dependency, corruption and stagnation; she claims that aid has undermined Africa's incentive to develop its own economic and political systems.

a846.speaker: Mark Toner, U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a846.speech: During the official handover of the consignment at the LRA Headquarters in Paynesville, reaffirmed the U.S. Government's commitment to supporting Liberia's revenue mobilization efforts as a cornerstone for national development ; "As Liberia transitions from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to the Value Added Tax (VAT) system, this equipment will play a pivotal role in improving operational efficiency and accountability, while also fostering public trust in the LRA" ; Emphasized that a robust tax administration system is fundamental to any nation's development: "By boosting the LRA's capacity to collect taxes more effectively, the United States is not only helping to increase revenue but also supporting the enhancement of public services in key sectors such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure" ; Further highlighted the importance of transparency and accountability in revenue management, stating that citizens must see the tangible benefits of their taxes to build confidence in the system.

a846.speaker: James Dorbor Jallah, LRA Commissioner General
a846.speech: Expressed profound gratitude to USAID for the generous donation and reiterated the LRA's commitment to its ambitious goal of increasing domestic revenue from US$700 million to US$1 billion in the near future ; "This support from USAID will significantly bolster our efforts to modernize our systems and improve tax collection, which is crucial for Liberia's development agenda" ; Acknowledged the long-standing contributions of the U.S. to Liberia's development in areas such as peace, security, health, and education, noting that the U.S.'s support is invaluable.

a882.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Egyptian Expatriates
a882.speech: Reaffirmed Egypt’s firm and supportive stand regarding Somalia’s security, stability, unity and territorial integrity ; also reaffirmed Egypt’s solidarity with the Somali government and people and backing for efforts to enhance the capacity of national Somali institutions and the gradual transfer of security responsibilities to the Somali security forces.

a882.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Egyptian Expatriates
a882.speech: Voiced Egypt’s concern over the ongoing security challenges posed by terrorist groups, particularly Al-Shabaab, stressing the importance of ensuring a smooth and coordinated transition from ATMIS to AUSSOM, and added that all steps are essential for preserving the security gains achieved so far and preventing security gaps that could be exploited.

a882.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Egyptian Expatriates
a882.speech: Underlined the importance of providing regular and sustainable funding for the AUSSOM to enable it to fully carry out its mandate, warning that failure to secure adequate funding would undermine the mission’s ability to perform its tasks and negatively affect the entire Horn of Africa and the international community, including disrupting global maritime trade routes and increasing terrorist threats.

a882.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Egyptian Expatriates
a882.speech: Emphasized Egypt’s commitment to supporting Somalia at both bilateral and multilateral levels through capacity-building programs, training personnel, supporting security and civil institutions and contributing to the provision of humanitarian assistance.

a957.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Candidate Country Report for FY 2026 (submitted to the U.S. Congress)
a957.speech: Revealed that Ghana has been declared ineligible to receive financial assistance from the MCC for fiscal year 2026; according to the report, Ghana’s ineligibility stems from a “debt default restriction” outlined in Section 7012 of the FY 2025 U.S. Appropriations Act, which prohibits assistance to countries with pending debt restructuring agreements ; the MCC noted: “Ghana is ineligible to receive foreign assistance pursuant to the debt default restriction… pending a debt restructuring agreement.” ; The MCC report clarified that Ghana’s status could change in the future if it resolves its ongoing debt restructuring process.

a985.speaker: Johannes Mururani, participant in the USAID Reach Namibia Project male engagement programme
a985.speech: Told the group he was a violent man until he attended a male engagement programme on gender norms under the USAID Reach Namibia Project, and is now adamant about creating a safe environment: "Imagine a world where boys and girls can walk safely to school without fear of violence. A world where women can make decisions about their health and bodies without coercion. A world where men and women stand together as equals, united in the fight against gender-based violence and HIV."

a985.speaker: Katamba Nanyemba, project coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a985.speech: Said there is ample evidence linking gender-based violence and HIV: "It shows us that survivors of violence have often limited control over their sexual health, face power imbalances that prevent them from negotiating safer sex, and fear stigma that deters them from accessing critical services."

a985.speaker: Bonifatius Wakudumo, Kavango East Governor
a985.speech: Told the group that it is their duty as men to educate themselves and others about GBV, its root causes, and its impact on individuals: "It is believed that five in six men are not abusers. But where are they? Can they stand up and be counted? Can the one in six who are abusers change their ways? Can we raise a new generation based on equality? Change is not easy, and it does not happen overnight. But every step we take today is a step toward building a safer and more equitable future. Let us be unwavering in our commitment and courageous in our actions."

a1142.speaker: Colonel Ali Hamani Hassane, Regional Director of Customs for Niamey-Tillabéri
a1142.speech: During an interview with the Nigerien Press Agency (ANP) on Wednesday 9 October 2024, revealed the impressive results of Operation Tsaron-Kassa: carried out between 16 July and 7 October 2024 by the Special Means of Transport Office, the initiative made it possible to mobilise 3.2 billion FCFA while strengthening security and contributing to the mobilisation of domestic resources to support the national economy in these difficult times, resulting in the impounding of 1,111 vehicles, 1,048 motorcycles and 104 tricycles, as well as the seizure of 254 jerrycans of 25 litres of petrol and 45,000 litres of diesel destined for illicit export to Mali.

a1142.speaker: Colonel Ali Hamani Hassane, Regional Director of Customs for Niamey-Tillabéri
a1142.speech: Commended the efforts of the Special Means of Transport Office, one of the 14 offices of the Niamey-Tillabéri regional directorate, for their crucial role in this mobilisation of domestic resources. He stressed the importance of complying with tax obligations when importing means of transport, recalling that these resources make it possible to finance the State's sovereign expenditures, including the security of the population.

a1142.speaker: Colonel Ali Hamani Hassane, Regional Director of Customs for Niamey-Tillabéri
a1142.speech: According to Colonel Ali Hamani, this operation is proving necessary to strengthen security in a context where insecurity prevails, making it difficult to identify those responsible for unregistered vehicles.

a1142.speaker: Colonel Ali Hamani Hassane, Regional Director of Customs for Niamey-Tillabéri
a1142.speech: During the interview, revealed that 543 cartons of illegally imported pharmaceutical products had been seized, as well as 490 cartons of shisha and 80 cartons of cigarettes, together with arrests for the sale of illicit fuel and drug use.

a1142.speaker: Colonel Ali Hamani Hassane, Regional Director of Customs for Niamey-Tillabéri
a1142.speech: The Regional Director stressed that the operation is continuing with "discipline, courtesy and firmness", regardless of the standing of the people involved.

a1142.speaker: Colonel Ali Hamani Hassane, Regional Director of Customs for Niamey-Tillabéri
a1142.speech: In conclusion, issued a call for civic-mindedness and responsibility from citizens, inviting them to take advantage of the opportunities offered to comply with the regulations.

a1143.speaker: USAID termination letter to implementing partners
a1143.speech: "Dear Implementing Partner, This award is being terminated for convenience and the interests of the U.S. Government pursuant to a directive from U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in his capacity as the Acting Administrator for the U.S. Agency for International Development ... and/or Peter W. Marocco... Secretary Rubio and PTDO Deputy Administrator Marocco have determined your award is not aligned with Agency priorities and made a determination that continuing this program is not in the national interest... Immediately cease all activities, terminate all subawards and contracts, and avoid incurring any additional obligations chargeable to the award beyond those unavoidable costs associated with this Termination Notice. Immediately provide similar instructions to all subrecipients and contractors. Kindly confirm receipt of this Termination Notice via electronic email response to the sender." Some organisations received emails, with attached letters, which were signed off with "thank you for partnering with USAID and God Bless America."

a1143.speaker: A senior Anova Health Institute official
a1143.speech: Confirmed to Bhekisisa that the Anova Health Institute, the organisation in South Africa which receives the most Pepfar funding, lost all its funding.

a1143.speaker: South African organisations
a1143.speech: Say they have also had reports from Pepfar-funded projects in Kenya and Malawi saying they had received similar letters.

a1143.speaker: A federal judge (US court order, February)
a1143.speech: Ordered the Trump administration in February to allow CDC-funded projects to restart their original projects.

a1143.speaker: Yvette Raphael, co-founder and co-director, Advocacy for Prevention of HIV and Aids (APHA)
a1143.speech: "We are deeply concerned about the bad decision to end USAID. The Trump administration has declared war on the right to health globally. The South African government must take this as an opportunity to expedite universal access to healthcare and meet its obligations to our people." ; "The NGO sector in South Africa woke to a letter from USAID terminating grants. It is so painful that these terminations mean death to poor people of the world. Key and vulnerable populations are the most affected... While the Trump administration is fighting for a land Bill that has nothing to do with them and making noise about human rights violations, they are inadvertently committing genocide that will be remembered for years to come. It is time for the world to speak up and call the Trump administration out for these unfair decisions. We need our government to step up at this moment in time, we need to hold their feet to the fire. The government must act swiftly and come up with a plan to save lives." ; "Saving dollars and spending lives - no words! We now really need to hear the plans from our country health departments how the chaos will be filled urgently."

a1143.speaker: An HIV clinician, speaking anonymously (17 years of Pepfar-supported work in health department clinics and hospitals)
a1143.speech: "Government has to cease the inaction and their seeming return to the behaviour we saw during the worst years of Aids denialism, where politicians let their own opinions impact hundreds of thousands of lives. This cannot be allowed to happen again." ; "Eight million South Africans rely on the government's antiretroviral HIV treatment programme and although Pepfar-funded organisations may only account for 17% of the budget, what they do with that 17% is so critical. Without it, and without an urgent plan to fill the gap, there is no doubt deaths will increase, people will suffer, babies will get infected and die... The SA government must now also be held to account to step in as we have seen with Nigeria and other African countries."

a1143.speaker: Fatima Hassan, founder, Health Justice Initiative
a1143.speech: "One expects a greater sense of urgency and better communication from the health ministry and other departments including the presidency in this time of crisis. They are downplaying the financial and human impact in South Africa, and that will not take us forward. As civil society we wrote in early February to the government, asking for its urgent plan, we got no response. We wrote again, and a month later we still await its urgent plan, which shockingly, we learnt from media reports that an assessment is being outsourced to Deloitte and will take a month or longer while right now there is a crisis! ... This is all going up in smoke because of the impact of the Trump administration's ideological executive orders and actions and its own defiance of court orders in the US - and because our government has no urgent plan to absorb staff, programmes, patients and communities. ... Government should answer - where is the money and where is the plan?"

a1143.speaker: Kholi Buthelezi, director, Sisonke
a1143.speech: "Sex workers are at increased risk for a range of health issues, including sexually transmitted infections (STIs), TB, HIV, and violence-related injuries. In South Africa, access to regular health screenings, education, and preventive care should be a basic right, not a privilege. When a major funding partner like USAID pulls its support, the ripple effects are felt throughout the entire ecosystem of services designed to support these individuals. This is why the government must step up now."

a1143.speaker: Anonymous HIV prevention programme implementer in Gauteng
a1143.speech: "Cutting USAID funding for health and education programmes in South Africa isn't just about budgets - it's about people. It's about sex workers who no longer have a safe place to get HIV prevention services, LGBTI+ communities losing the support they fought so hard for and thousands now facing a future without the healthcare and education they rely on to survive. These aren't just numbers on a spreadsheet. They are lives, futures, and communities being abandoned. The reality is heart breaking: People will suffer, people will die, and decades of progress will be undone. This is not just a funding cut - it's a betrayal of the very people these programmes were meant to protect. And yet, from the national health department, there is silence. No communication, no coordination, no urgency - just a deafening void where leadership should be... This silence is complicity, and it is costing lives."

a1143.speaker: Kate Rees, public health specialist
a1143.speech: "Our programmes have been officially terminated. Thousands of dedicated healthcare workers across South Africa have been retrenched. I am especially concerned for the community health workers and data capturers, who are financially vulnerable and won't be easily absorbed into the health system. Despite their years of commitment, these healthcare workers have been abandoned with almost no notice. For patients and communities, critical services have already been impacted - including following up on positive HIV tests for babies, following up on possible meningitis cases, and caring for the most vulnerable pregnant women whose babies are now at risk of contracting HIV."

a1143.speaker: Public health specialist (anonymous)
a1143.speech: "This is absolutely shattering, heartbreaking, and incomprehensible. The termination letters issued by the US state department in the last 24 hours mark the abrupt and devastating end to years - decades - of investment in lifesaving programmes that have transformed communities, saved countless lives, and built essential infrastructure for health, education, and development. The intellectual capital, expertise, and dedication poured into these programmes have simply been erased by bureaucratic decisions made overnight. How do you quantify the loss of a child's access to malaria treatment? A mother's TB medication? A community's clean water project? The people - the patients, the frontline workers, the programme recipients who relied on these services for survival - are now left stranded, abandoned by a system that once promised progress and partnership. Every contract cancelled is not just a number; it represents a life, a community, a future now in jeopardy."

a1166.speaker: Coulibaly and Fontagne, researchers (study 'South-South Trade')
a1166.speech: As shown in the study they published under the title 'South-South Trade', if landlocked African countries' port access were increased by ten percent, their annual export performance would grow on average by twenty percent.

a1166.speaker: World Bank (2014 study)
a1166.speech: A study carried out by the World Bank in 2014 shows that, compared with African countries that have ports, landlocked ones face logistics costs in international trade that are three times higher.

a1166.speaker: Djankov and Freund, researchers (study 'Trading On Time')
a1166.speech: As the result of the study they published under the title 'Trading On Time' states, because of the trade delays landlocked countries' products face in connection with customs services, their exports decline by one percent for each day of delay.

a1166.speaker: World Bank (study)
a1166.speech: As the World Bank study result shows, Ethiopia, which is landlocked and conducts 95 percent of its international trade through the port of Djibouti, sees its importers and exporters exposed to various additional costs because of the bureaucratic problems created by customs procedures that the Djiboutian government changes from time to time; as a result Ethiopia incurs an additional cost of between 1.5 and two billion dollars every year.

a1166.speaker: United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) (2017 research report)
a1166.speech: According to the results of the research report released by UNIDO in 2017, in Ethiopia the time taken to transport export products and deliver them to consumers is delayed by weeks because of the port problem.

a1166.speaker: International Coffee Organization (ICO) and National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) (studies)
a1166.speech: As studies conducted by the ICO and the NBE have indicated, manufacturers engaged in textile production in the industrial parks have been subjected to various penalties (mainly being required to give price discounts) because they were unable to supply their products to the international market on the ordered schedule.

a1166.speaker: Brookings Institution (2021 study)
a1166.speech: As the result of a study conducted in 2021 by the Brookings Institution indicates, because of port logistics delays the foreign exchange Ethiopia should have earned from coffee exports in 2021 fell by 18 percent.

a1166.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (2018 study)
a1166.speech: As shown in a study carried out in 2018 by USAID, the average transport and logistics cost for coffee exporters in Ethiopia amounts to 28 percent of the income they earn from coffee sales.

a1166.speaker: Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) and McKinsey & Co (2020 joint study)
a1166.speech: As the result of the study jointly conducted in 2020 by the EIC and McKinsey & Co shows, because textile manufacturers find it difficult to supply their products to the international market on time due to the port problem, they are forced to use air transport or air cargo, which is four times more expensive than sea transport, greatly reducing their revenue and profitability.

a1166.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) (2020 study report)
a1166.speech: As stated in the study report issued by UNCTAD in 2020, Ethiopia's port access problem has caused transport and logistics costs to amount to between 40 and 50 percent of the price of imported goods, whereas for African countries with ports the figure is only between 10 and 20 percent.

a1166.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) (2020 'Review of Maritime Transport')
a1166.speech: As the study released by UNCTAD in 2020 under the title 'Review of Maritime Transport' indicated, if the port-related problems faced by landlocked countries such as Ethiopia, Rwanda and Zambia were resolved, it would enable their economies to grow by an average of two percent.

a1166.speaker: Rodrigue, Notteboom and Pallis, researchers (2020 study)
a1166.speech: As the study result they published in 2020 indicates, port services strengthen other trade-related economic activities such as the logistics, manufacturing and service sectors.

a1166.speaker: Arvis, Raballand and Marteau, researchers (2010 study 'The Cost of Being Landlocked')
a1166.speech: As shown in the study they published in 2010 under the title 'The Cost of Being Landlocked', because landlocked countries' transport and logistics costs are high, and their production costs therefore rise, their goods become expensive on the international market.

a1166.speaker: Limao and Venables, researchers (study)
a1166.speech: As the researchers confirmed in their study, landlocked countries' transport and logistics costs are 50 percent higher compared with countries that have ports.

a1166.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (2020 report)
a1166.speech: As UNCTAD warned in its 2020 report, Ethiopia's dependence on the port of Djibouti has placed the country's economy under strategic risk and therefore an urgent solution to the problem is needed, it said.

a1166.speaker: Habtamu Girma Demissie, research fellow at the African Economic Research Consortium (AERC) and PhD researcher, University of Ibadan (author)
a1166.speech: Argues that resolving Ethiopia's sea-access question has a value that goes beyond the economy to rescuing the country's national security from danger, and that it is homework that cannot be left until tomorrow for all the countries of the Horn of Africa to understand Ethiopia's sea-access question in this light and to seek solutions by which the country can obtain a port peacefully.

a1192.speaker: Simon Namesho, University of Namibia (Unam) spokesperson
a1192.speech: Said another initiative, the Improving Rural Quality Education in Namibia and Iowa project, valued at approximately N$1.5 million, was also affected; highlighted that most of the university's current projects are funded by partners in Canada, Japan, the European Union and Namibia itself. "While some of our partners have been impacted by the US funding freeze, Unam's current research is largely unaffected, as our major funding comes from other sources." ; "For example, our Group for Research in Infectious Diseases is funded by the UK, the EU and the German government."

a1192.speaker: Simon Namesho, Unam spokesperson
a1192.speech: Acknowledged that the cancelled US grant has disrupted plans for a postgraduate conference and affected some School of Education partnerships. "We are in dialogue with African institutions and partners to coordinate responses to these funding challenges."

a1192.speaker: Simon Namesho, Unam spokesperson
a1192.speech: Noted that the university is strengthening collaborations with European institutions and aligning itself with global research platforms such as the European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership (EDCTP). "Namibia has formalised its association with the EDCTP, which enhances our eligibility for international health research funding."

a1192.speaker: Simon Namesho, Unam spokesperson
a1192.speech: "We are currently assessing the full impact and will report once the process is complete." ; Added that Unam will be represented at the upcoming EDCTP annual general meeting in Kigali in June.

a1192.speaker: Namibian Sun (previous reporting)
a1192.speech: Recently reported on the Fulbright scholarships and several US-supported health, education and conservation programmes that have been suspended or delayed as Washington reassesses its foreign funding priorities.

a1192.speaker: Civil society organisations
a1192.speech: Warn that the aid freeze jeopardises essential services for communities affected by HIV, youth unemployment and environmental degradation.

a1327.speaker: Coordination Unit for the formulation of the 2nd programme and monitoring of reforms of MCA-Benin (UCF/MCA-Bénin)
a1327.speech: Confirmed, before the press on Thursday 18 December, Benin's eligibility for the 2nd compact, presenting the content of the programme for the coming five years as well as the benefits Benin can draw from it.

a1327.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Bénin
a1327.speech: Visibly pleased to see Benin once again selected for the MCC compact, first expressed the Beninese government's gratitude to the American people and their government ; then praised the resourcefulness of the United States Ambassador to Benin in bringing the matter to a successful conclusion ; confirming Benin's eligibility, recalled that it was the corruption indicator that was in the red and caused the country to be rejected, specifying that the decision last year was taken unanimously, but that this year, thanks to the progress made by everyone and above all the anti-corruption plan put in place by the government, the country achieved this positive result that brings a smile to everyone's face today ; said that Benin had never previously passed more than 11 indicators, and that this year it achieved the feat of passing 12, adding that "if everyone does their bit, if there are more efforts, Benin can pass 13 or even 14 indicators."

a1327.speaker: Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of UCF/MCA-Bénin
a1327.speech: Explained the amount of the funds: "a base envelope of 250 million US dollars," specifying that Ghana had a base envelope of 300 million dollars, but that with the flexibility of the Americans and the support of its private sector, the envelope rose to 500 million US dollars. "Benin can do as much. It all depends on us."

a1327.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, MCC Deputy Vice-President
a1327.speech: "If we can supply more electricity, that can unleash the engine of growth in Benin," underlining in passing the need to build an attractive framework in order to attract investment from everyone. "This will require enormous efforts on the part of MCC and commitments on the part of the government of Benin." ; Added that he hoped this would help make the dreams of the Beninese people lasting ; invited everyone to make progress and go beyond the progress achieved by Ghana, hoping the private sector would seize the opportunity to do as the Ghanaians did ; "There are today new technologies that can help reduce electricity consumption. If a stable institutional framework is put in place, that can attract the private sector."

a1327.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, MCC Deputy Vice-President
a1327.speech: On MCC's own stake in signing the compact with Benin, specified that it is "just so that there is a fairer, freer and more prosperous world. That is the whole interest of the USA."

a1327.speaker: The speakers at the press conference (Samuel Batcho, Christopher Broughton and Jonathan Bloom)
a1327.speech: Dwelt on the content of the Programme, which they say will be exclusively concentrated on the energy sector in Benin, a sector they describe as strategic for the country's development ; in response to many press questions on what will concretely be done in Benin's energy sector, were very precise in assuring that feasibility studies will be carried out.

a1456.speaker: Lawyers for Venezuelan men in US immigration custody
a1456.speech: Said they were at imminent risk of removal without the judicial review previously mandated by the justices, prompting the US Supreme Court on 19 April to temporarily bar Trump's administration from deporting them.

a1456.speaker: Trump administration
a1456.speech: Has alleged that the Venezuelans are members of the Tren de Aragua criminal gang.

a1456.speaker: Family members and lawyers for the migrants
a1456.speech: Have disputed the administration's allegation that the Venezuelans are members of the Tren de Aragua criminal gang.

a1456.speaker: Federal judge overseeing the case of a Salvadoran man living in Maryland
a1456.speech: Rebuked the government for trying to circumvent an order blocking additional deportations and misleading the court about its actions.

a1456.speaker: Two other federal judges (in deportation cases under the Alien Enemies Act)
a1456.speech: Voiced doubts about the legality of the administration's moves and temporarily barred it from removing additional detainees while they consider longer-lasting orders.

a1456.speaker: Challengers to Trump's birthright citizenship executive order
a1456.speech: Argued that Trump's order violates a right enshrined in the US Constitution's 14th Amendment that provides that anyone born in the United States is a citizen.

a1456.speaker: Some conservatives
a1456.speech: Have argued that diversity, equity and inclusion policies discriminate against white people and certain others.

a1456.speaker: Plaintiffs in lawsuits challenging Trump's tariffs
a1456.speech: The suits accuse Trump of overstepping his authority under the Constitution by imposing the duties without congressional authorization.

a1687.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a1687.speech: At the start of the session, prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died, offered his condolences to their families and wished a prompt recovery to the injured, following the tragedies that occurred at the gold-panning sites at Kokoyo, in the village of Danga, Kangaba Cercle, and at Bilalikoto, Kenieba Cercle. He instructed the Government to strengthen measures to avoid human and environmental tragedies in the country.

a1687.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a1687.speech: Further instructed: the repeal of the appointment orders of the administrative officials directly involved in the occurrence of the said incidents (Prefect, Sub-prefects, heads of the Security Forces - Police, Gendarmerie, Guard - of the local Water and Forestry services, the Sanitation and Pollution and Nuisance Control services, and the sub-regional Geology and Mines services); the revision of certain legal texts in order, among other things, to put an end to settlements in the environmental field, to facilitate the recovery of equipment involved in gold panning and its transfer to state property; the suspension of artisanal mining exploitation permits granted to persons of foreign nationality; and the launch of the procedure to dissolve the communal council of Dabia.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a1687.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted draft texts relating to the ratification of the budget support agreement including a loan, signed in Bamako on 26 February 2025 between the Government of the Republic of Mali and the Qatar Fund for Development, under which the Fund grants Mali budget support of 50 million US dollars, about 31.4475 billion CFA francs, comprising a loan of 45 million US dollars; this budget support will help sustain the humanitarian aid, economic development and health sectors, notably the supply of foodstuffs, the construction of water points, the rehabilitation and construction of infrastructure and the strengthening of the means of action of the Administration and local authorities.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a1687.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordinance amending Law No. 06-067 of 29 December 2006, as amended, on the General Tax Code, modifying articles 240 and 425 to adapt the General Tax Code to the new Mining Code, extending the scope of the Special Tax on Certain Products to marble, gold ingots and other mining products, reducing the minimum rate of that tax for those products from 5% to 3%, and extending stamp duty on export intentions to all mining products.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a1687.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree setting the deadlines and procedures for concluding agreements between the National Health Insurance Fund and health providers; a draft decree approving the standard management-delegation agreements under the Universal Health Insurance Scheme; and a draft decree setting the principles of preferential pricing and the coverage rates for health care services under the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of Mali's participation in the "High-Level Segment" on the human rights situation, held from 24 to 26 February 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland, where Mali addressed the Human Rights Council with strong messages: reaffirmation of the Government's determination to implement all the recommendations accepted during the Universal Periodic Review and the commitments made at the high-level event "Human Rights 75"; the remarkable improvement in the overall security situation thanks to the efforts of the Armed and Security Forces and their strategic partners; the pooling of defence resources by the Heads of State of the Alliance of Sahel States in order to fight terrorism effectively; the appropriation of the endogenous resolution of multidimensional crises through the ongoing drafting of the National Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation; the Government's determination to fight impunity in all its forms; the reiteration of the appeal to the international community to avoid the politicisation and instrumentalisation of human rights; and the reaffirmation of the Government of Mali's willingness to continue its cooperation with all human rights promotion and protection mechanisms, in strict respect for its sovereignty and the vital interests of the Malian people. On the margins of the High-Level Segment, the minister had an audience with the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights on Mali's efforts and progress in human rights and the resumption and strengthening of cooperative relations between Mali and the Office of the High Commissioner.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his mission to Timbuktu from 25 to 27 February 2025, whose objectives included assessing the state of progress of the operationalisation of the University of Timbuktu, exchanging with administrative, customary and educational authorities, and visiting the site earmarked for the construction of the University's infrastructure. He reported that the department had appointed a Coordinator in charge of operationalisation activities, renovated certain administrative and teaching premises and held the first session of the Board of Directors of the Ahmed Baba Institute of Higher Islamic Studies and Research of Timbuktu, and that the mission noted with interest and satisfaction the progress of the operationalisation process and the involvement of the actors concerned.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers about the student meetings called "Citizen Masterclass", organised with the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research as a mission of civic and citizenship education, personal development and patriotic engagement to make students "model and responsible citizens", consisting of the minister delivering modules on citizenship in public or private universities during the 2025 academic year in order to strengthen the role of students in the refoundation of Mali.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his participation in the 19th edition of the National Cereals Exchange, launched officially from 19 to 21 February 2025, whose objective was to contribute to the promotion and valorisation of locally produced cereals; the 2025 edition recorded the signing of 61 contracts for a total of 1,184,410,000 CFA francs, against 261 contracts worth 1,070,988,394 CFA francs for the 2024 edition, and recommendations were formulated for the Ministry of Agriculture, the Food Security Commission and the Permanent Assembly of Chambers of Agriculture of Mali.

a1687.speaker: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the launch of the recruitment process for unemployed young graduates for the 14th contingent of the vocational training internship programme of the Agency for the Promotion of Youth Employment, with the recruitment of 2,500 new interns beginning with a call for applications on 13 February 2025 and the opening of application submissions on 17 February 2025; by the closing date of 22 February 2025, 15,021 applications had been registered nationwide, comprising 6,791 male applications (45.22%) and 8,230 female applications (54.78%), with new interns to be assigned to the Institutions of the Republic, ministerial departments, local authorities, consular and umbrella organisations and non-governmental organisations.

a1687.speaker: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of a field mission to the Gao Region from 27 February to 1 March 2025 to convey to local populations the message of comfort, reassurance and solidarity of the Transition Authorities and to gather their priority needs in skills development and socio-professional integration, particularly for young people and women; activities included the inauguration of a new building for the Regional Directorate of Employment and Vocational Training, the opening of three Youth Guidance Spaces, the launch of the "driving licence" operation and the handover of integration kits to training beneficiaries. The mission also gathered the expectations of local actors, which include the continuation of peace and security initiatives, adapting training provision to labour market needs, specific support for young people and women, and the introduction of concrete measures to reduce unemployment.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the holding in Mali of the 1st edition of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation's Africa Investment Forum, decided at the 47th Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers held on 27 and 28 November 2020 in Niger, with Mali selected to host the 2025 event at the 50th Session held in August 2024 in Yaounde, Cameroon. The forum, on the theme "Unlocking investment potential in Africa", aims to strengthen economic cooperation within the OIC and attract investors to Africa, will address themes such as investment financing, insurance and gender issues, and offers Mali an opportunity to promote its economic attractiveness and mobilise public and private investment.

a1687.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a1687.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the country's epidemiological situation, marked by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with the previous week.

a1687.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a1687.speech: Called on the population to strictly respect the measures for the prevention of and fight against dengue.

a1761.speaker: Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Announced that the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement will officially begin next week, on Meskerem 29, 2018 E.C., and that Ethiopia will send its first shipment to Kenya. The Ministry stated this at a press briefing given on Monday, Meskerem 19, 2018 E.C., marking the conclusion of the 6th Working Party meeting of the World Trade Organization accession negotiations held recently in Geneva, the capital of Switzerland.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Said that although the African Continental Free Trade Area agreement had been expected to be officially launched in the second week of Meskerem, it did not begin because of the World Trade Organization membership negotiations, and that the agreement will therefore begin to be implemented next week, on Meskerem 29, 2018 E.C. "Officially launching the agreement is an easy task," the minister said, explaining that implementing new multilateral agreements is the difficult and challenging part and requires a great deal of work.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Indicated that the process will begin with trade in goods or commodities with the countries that have signed the agreement, and noted that a request to conclude an agreement in the services sector has been submitted but that the negotiation has not been completed. He noted that since the negotiation request submitted to the WTO is handled in this same forum, nothing different is expected to emerge, and the negotiation is expected to be concluded this year. He said the revenue to be obtained cannot be stated now, but that it will be seen going forward in the course of implementation.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Noted that 34 countries have approved the Goods Offer in their councils of ministers, and said that under the agreement, organizations importing products from these countries will, if they come with a Rules of Origin certificate, be allowed to bring them in duty-free, and the Customs Commission will issue them certificates and serve them. He did not fail to mention that private companies are asking for the process to be put into operation quickly and that they want to trade under this framework, because they are missing opportunities to export products under the agreement.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Explained the activities carried out toward WTO membership at the 6th Working Party meeting; said that at present 22 countries are at various stages of negotiation to join the WTO, and that of these Ethiopia and Uzbekistan are close to membership. He said that over the five months since the 5th Working Party meeting much work was done and extensive preparation was made for the 6th Working Party meeting, including an Ethiopia WTO Forum in which more than 30 member countries participated, and productive discussions with countries friendly to Ethiopia.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Explained that at the 6th Working Party about 30 of the organization's member countries and the World Bank spoke in support of Ethiopia's WTO membership; that Ethiopia's negotiating committee submitted a factual document of more than 650 pages and the plenary decided that the document should be advanced to the draft report stage for approval, which is a major achievement; and that more than 200 questions were raised and answered at the meeting. He said 54 additional legal documents were submitted at this meeting and that the total submitted to date has reached 398.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Noted that alongside the Working Party meeting, face-to-face discussions were held with about 14 of the 22 member countries that had requested bilateral market access negotiations, that agreement was reached at the technical level with six of them, and that four countries withdrew from the negotiations for various reasons. The minister said Russia, China, Türkiye, Argentina and Thailand are among the countries with which agreement was reached, but refrained from disclosing the names of the countries that withdrew from the negotiations.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: "When a country that has requested bilateral market access negotiations does not move at your pace, you run into difficulty; you send it a document and it says it will not respond, it delays. On the other hand, there are cases where they ask you to lower what you have offered below the stated standard." He noted that this is a challenge of the accession process, but said that, based on the experience gained with the six countries with which agreement was reached, work will be done to complete negotiations conducted on the principle of give and take.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Indicated that the negotiations with Switzerland and Japan could be concluded next week, and said work will be done to reach agreement, by Hidar 30, 2018 E.C., with the 14 countries with which active negotiations are underway. He added that the multilateral and bilateral trade negotiations with the United States have not yet been concluded and are continuing in a strengthened manner, and that multilateral negotiations will continue alongside bilateral market access talks.

a1761.speaker: Kassahun Gofe (PhD), Minister of Trade and Regional Integration of Ethiopia
a1761.speech: Emphasized that the advancement of Ethiopia's factual report to the Working Party draft report stage is promising for the ongoing WTO membership process; noted that the 6th Working Party meeting concluded successfully; and announced that the 7th Working Party meeting has been scheduled for Tir 2018 E.C., and that work is under way with a plan to conclude the WTO negotiations at the organization's 14th Ministerial Conference to be held in Cameroon in March 2026.

a1790.speaker: Janira Borges, 32, campaign activist in Ponta d'Água who normally works in the informal sector
a1790.speech: "Normally I sell clothes, shoes and other products to earn a living, but I decided to suspend that activity and work as an activist out of love for the party" ; recounted that before the campaigns began she sought out the party official in her neighbourhood and made herself available to work; he wrote down her name and referred her to another official who later contacted her ; "I like this work, I do it out of love for the party and I still earn something. The majority of us who work as activists do it out of love for the party."

a1790.speaker: José António Pereira, 35, campaign activist in Ponta d'Água, blacksmith and funeral-home worker
a1790.speech: "I am here more out of love than for the money. Even if they did not pay, if I had free time I would still help" ; "I know that I will be able to buy something for my son, even if simple, just by putting up posters and mobilising voters to support my candidate."

a1790.speaker: Santinho, resident of Eugénio Lima who rented his house as a party campaign headquarters
a1790.speech: "I decided to rent out the ground floor because the house had been closed for some time, more than a year in fact. Before that, I had rented it to someone to open a bar, but my daughter complained a lot about the noise, since she lives on the first floor, so I preferred it to stay closed until someone appeared wanting to rent it for something other than a bar" ; "It is a two-bedroom house, with a kitchen, a bathroom and a large living room. We decided to rent the house for only 20 thousand escudos. It is not much money, but at least it will help in some way" ; noted that when renting the space the party was aware it would have to take out an electricity contract, since many rent a house and leave debts that then have to be paid ; "They are also aware that they cannot stick posters on the walls, unless it is with very weak tape so as not to damage them, since I painted recently."

a1790.speaker: Marcos Silva, driver of a campaign vehicle in Achada Santo António, hired by his father-in-law
a1790.speech: Recounted that his father-in-law owns the vehicle, the generator and the sound equipment, but since he cannot be at the wheel for hours on end he hired Marcos; Marcos cannot specify how much his father-in-law charges for the vehicle and the sound equipment, but, for example, the generator rental costs two thousand escudos a day and the party has to pay for the fuel used every day ; "I have to be in the car at 08:00 and I stay until 12:30, then I take a lunch break and come back at 14:00 until around 18:30" ; "On the 29th, my father-in-law pays for my service. Even if it is little, it will be enough for a better Christmas" ; "Normally I work, but only when it comes up, and what I am going to earn with this work is more than I normally earn. I earn little."

a1790.speaker: Luísa Lobo, head of Tipografia Santos (printing house)
a1790.speech: Explained that when candidacies decide to have this type of work done in the country, it means an increase in sales in that period ; "The increase in sales does not necessarily lead us to hire more people for the work, unless it coincides with other seasonal jobs in which the volume increases considerably" ; revealed that in this campaign production was organised during a period of low demand, which made it possible to meet the orders without needing to reinforce the team ; lamented the narrow profit margin: "Nowadays profits are not large in any work because production costs are almost always high, the price of raw materials has risen a lot at source and clients are not very receptive when we want to increase the final price" ; said that since July the printing house began contacting the parties to find out their intentions about whether or not to have the work done in the country, in order to plan imports and build stock, since there are no local suppliers for large quantities of the necessary raw materials ; "Recently they got in touch and, even without stock, we turned to suppliers for small quantities, adjusting what we had" ; said many parties choose to place part of their orders outside Cabo Verde, claiming limitations of the domestic market: "If everything that can possibly be produced were made in the country, even with a small price difference, we would all work with much more breathing room."

a1790.speaker: Cláudio Correia, known as DJ 100 Juiz, music and image producer in Assomada
a1790.speech: "I have worked with electoral campaigns since 2004, it is an extra that pays off, but it is very frustrating because it demands a lot, everything has to be immediate" ; said the short deadline for delivering materials affects the workload and the price of the work: "A campaign song has to be made in one hour, whereas for other jobs it would take three days. That requires us to suspend other projects and justifies the additional cost" ; pointed to the risk of late payments, an experience that led him to formalise his services this year, securing contracts for greater protection: "Payment is made 50% before and 50% after the elections. If the party does not win, it is very complicated to receive what remains. Before, I did not turn to any entity that would compel them to pay, first because I worked informally and worked without contracts, there was no proof that I had done that work."

a1790.speaker: Ailton Moreira, economist
a1790.speech: Explained that political parties and candidates need financial support to fund electoral activities, with the main revenues coming from their own funds, contributions from sympathisers, bank loans and State subsidies ; cited as an example that in the last legislative and presidential elections it is estimated that public subsidies generated an amount of around 10 million euros for activities such as rallies, marches and advertising campaigns, moving sectors such as transport, food, events and street commerce ; said street vendors, rental transport and entertainment sectors such as music and theatre come to the fore in this period, and that the circulation of money intensifies for between ten and 30 days, contributing to local economic dynamism ; "Artists and activists gain visibility and skills that can be used in future employment opportunities."

a1790.speaker: Ailton Moreira, economist
a1790.speech: Said that notwithstanding the positive effects, the long-term impact is limited and depends on the promises made by the candidates and their fulfilment after the elections: "The activities generated by the campaigns can serve as experience for the local private sector and project future initiatives, but this is directly related to the public policies implemented after the electoral period" ; suggested that, in order to maximise the economic impact of campaigns, these should be channelled into strengthening the local economy in a sustainable way, taking advantage of the skills acquired and encouraging innovation in the sectors that benefit.

a1790.speaker: Electoral Code of Cabo Verde (document)
a1790.speech: Establishes that the revenues of electoral campaigns may come from political parties, State subsidies, donations from citizens and national companies, voters abroad, campaign activities, contributions from candidates and loans from national credit institutions; that revenues must be documented and submitted; and that the State subsidy, allocated by the National Elections Commission (CNE), varies according to the type of election and is calculated per valid vote — seven hundred and fifty escudos for each validly expressed vote in presidential and legislative elections, and five hundred escudos in municipal elections, the latter to be revised regularly taking into account accumulated inflation.

a1790.speaker: National Elections Commission (CNE) (reported expenditure data)
a1790.speech: In the 2020 municipal elections, in terms of expenditure reported to the CNE, the MpD had the largest expenditure (130.5 million escudos), followed by the PAICV (105.6 million) and the UCID (12.8 million), followed by other parties such as the PP, LUTA and DSB with smaller amounts.

a1802.speaker: United Nations
a1802.speech: According to the United Nations, 735 million people suffer from hunger in the world, one person in five on the African continent.

a1802.speaker: Catherine Colonna, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (opinion piece)
a1802.speech: Argues that the most vulnerable countries, those already bearing the full brunt of the consequences of the war in Ukraine, will pay the heaviest price following the abrupt halt of the Black Sea agreements, and that this halt is irresponsible at a time when 2022 was a terrible year for food security; states that the end of the initiative will mean a significant reduction in the volumes of grain reaching the populations that need it most, and that the donations announced by Russia, without any precise date and limited to a handful of countries and a few thousand tonnes, represent a tiny fraction of the humanitarian aid provided via the Black Sea by the World Food Programme: "This minimal and cosmetic gesture, displayed on the occasion of a Summit, fools no one."

a1802.speaker: Catherine Colonna, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (opinion piece)
a1802.speech: Warns that the abrupt termination of the agreements by Russia will make grain prices even more volatile, and that prices remain very high, having seen their sharpest increase on 19 July, with a risk of further rises in the medium term; argues that Russia and its agricultural sector profit from the increase, seeking to enrich themselves at the expense of the most destitute while their exports are subject to no sanctions.

a1802.speaker: Catherine Colonna, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (opinion piece)
a1802.speech: Accuses Russia of deliberately striking the ports of Odesa, Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk, destroying grain silos and firing on civilian ships, thereby openly violating international law and destroying reserves destined for the World Food Programme, making food a weapon: "Making hunger a weapon of political coercion, that is the point to which Russia has sunk. Once again, as it has done constantly for a year and a half, it violates an elementary principle of our common morality."

a1802.speaker: Catherine Colonna, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France (opinion piece)
a1802.speech: States that France and its European partners have chosen the path of responsibility and international solidarity; that France mobilised more than 840 million euros in food aid nationally over the past year, including nearly 250 million euros in emergency aid; that it contributes to the European Union's "solidarity corridors", which have allowed more than 38 million tonnes of grain to be exported from Ukraine by road, rail and river; and that while Russia reduced its contribution to the World Food Programme, France gave it strengthened financial and material support. "France will continue its efforts, notably in October in Paris on the occasion of the summit of the coalition for school meals... In the face of this, France will act tirelessly, with its partners, so that those who need it most can feed themselves properly. We, for our part, will remain faithful to our principles."

a1806.speaker: Executive Mansion (press release), Liberia
a1806.speech: Says the over ninety thousand U.S. Dollars allocated funds will go towards enhancing the learning conditions of primary and secondary schools across the country; President Boakai, in the release, directed the Civil Service Agency to collaborate with the Ministry of Finance in establishing an escrow account to maximize the impact of said funds.

a1806.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a1806.speech: Believes that this move reinforces the government's commitment to upholding integrity in public service, while prioritizing policies that directly benefit the citizens, especially school-going children; has ordered the Civil Service Agency (CSA) to work closely with the Ministry of Education to fully implement the "One Child, One Chair Presidential Initiative".

a1806.speaker: Josiah Joekai, Director General of the Civil Service Agency (CSA), Liberia
a1806.speech: Told ELBC on Tuesday, March 18, 2025, that, as mandated by the President, the over 90 thousand US Dollars collected from the salaries of officials who did not declare their assets will go toward the program; also disclosed that an escrow account was opened at the Central Bank of Liberia, where the money for the project is being deposited.

a1892.speaker: Aga Khan Development Network (statement)
a1892.speech: A statement issued by his charitable organisation, the Aga Khan Development Network, said the leader died peacefully in Lisbon, Portugal, with his family.

a1892.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a1892.speech: “I received with great sadness the news of the death of Prince Karim Al-Husseini, Aga Khan IV, the supreme spiritual leader of the Ismaili Muslim denomination worldwide and founder of the Aga Khan Development Network. On behalf of the Government of the United Republic of Tanzania, I offer condolences to the family of Prince Aga Khan, the Aga Khan Development Network and the Ismaili Muslim Community. We join you in mourning the loss of a great and visionary leader, whose work has touched the lives of millions of people around the world,” she wrote on her social media pages.

a1892.speaker: Dr William Ruto, President of Kenya (post on X)
a1892.speech: “He was a great leader who went far by doing what was thought impossible; he did it by helping vulnerable communities, through voluntary and charitable activities, through the building of schools and hospitals. We are deeply saddened by the death of His Highness the Aga Khan, the spiritual leader of the Ismaili Muslims… We are with the prince's family and the Ismaili community as a whole,” he said.

a1892.speaker: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General (through UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric)
a1892.speech: Said he remembered His Highness the Aga Khan IV as a global spiritual leader and an advocate of peace, development and solidarity. “For decades the Aga Khan devoted himself to improving the well-being of people's lives around the world, especially those at risk of lacking humanitarian services, by supporting access to education and cultural assistance,” ; “The leadership of the Aga Khan institution went far beyond the faith of the Shia Ismaili denomination. He was a bridge educating us between culture and world development. His efforts to fight poverty, bring gender equality and spur sustainable development are among the marks he left us.”

a1892.speaker: The book 'The Divine Kingship of the Aga Khan: A Study of Theocracy in East Africa'
a1892.speech: According to the book, the Aga Khan is described as a direct descendant of the Prophet Muhammad through his cousin and son-in-law, Ali, whom the Nizari Ismailis recognise as Imam, along with his wife Fatima, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad from his first marriage.

a1892.speaker: Aga Khan IV (Prince Karim Al-Hussaini), 49th Imam of the Shia Ismailis
a1892.speech: After taking over the imamate, declared his intention to continue the work his grandfather had begun of building modern institutions, in order to improve the lives of others ; during the Takht Nashini period (1957–1958) he stressed the importance of maintaining good relations between different communities — a message that carried great meaning because of the ethnic tensions that existed in East Africa at the time, between black people and South Asians.

a1892.speaker: Aga Khan IV (Prince Karim Al-Hussaini), 49th Imam of the Shia Ismailis
a1892.speech: Asked his long-time friend, the Prime Minister of Canada, Pierre Trudeau, for help after Asians, including Nizari Ismailis, were expelled from Uganda in 1972 ; urged Nizari Ismailis living in developed nations to contribute to community development in developing countries through various development projects.

a2113.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2113.speech: Warned on Wednesday that violent clashes around the Zamzam camp for displaced persons in North Darfur are disrupting the delivery of humanitarian aid and endangering the safety of civilians, and that the fighting is jeopardising the arrival of the WFP's vital convoys in the camp, where famine is officially confirmed.

a2113.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2113.speech: "These deliveries are the only way to reverse the trend of famine," it said on the social network X, expressing its deep concern for the safety of civilians in the camp and of its partners on the ground ; said it currently has no staff in the location but succeeded in delivering, on 22 November, aid intended for 12,500 people, the first distribution in several months, the convoy leaving the camp on 29 November after distributing all of the aid.

a2113.speaker: United Nations
a2113.speech: Firmly condemned on Tuesday the deadly bombardments of Zamzam, the largest site for displaced persons in Darfur.

a2113.speaker: Clementine Nkweta-Salami, UN Resident Coordinator in Sudan
a2113.speech: Expressed her "deep concern" at the attacks of 1 and 2 December, which killed at least five people and injured 18 others, forcing the evacuation of a hospital and the suspension of health services in the camp ; recalled: "Civilians and civilian infrastructure are protected by international humanitarian law and should never be targeted."

a2113.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2113.speech: According to OCHA, famine could persist in besieged areas, notably in Zamzam, during the 2025 lean season if aid remains obstructed, and extreme food insecurity also affects other regions such as South Kordofan and Khartoum, where thousands of displaced civilians are in danger.

a2113.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) and the United Nations
a2113.speech: Are calling for immediate and unimpeded access for humanitarian aid in order to avoid a worsening of the humanitarian catastrophe.

a2118.speaker: 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for the DRC
a2118.speech: Announced on Thursday, aims to deliver lifesaving assistance to 11 million Congolese, including 7.8 million internally displaced persons, and includes treating 1.5 million children suffering from acute malnutrition, providing access to safe drinking water for five million people, and combating outbreaks of diseases such as cholera, measles, and Mpox.

a2118.speaker: Bruno Lemarquis, UN Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC
a2118.speech: "All warning signals are flashing red. Yet, despite immense challenges, humanitarian action continues to prove its effectiveness in saving lives every day" ; "We must adapt to keep delivering this vital aid without ever compromising the fundamental principles that guide humanitarian action: neutrality, impartiality, independence, and humanity."

a2118.speaker: Bruno Lemarquis, UN Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC
a2118.speech: "We stand at a crossroads. Without increased international mobilization, humanitarian needs will skyrocket, regional stability will be further jeopardized and our capacity to respond will be severely compromised."

a2118.speaker: Bruno Lemarquis, UN Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC
a2118.speech: "Humanitarian assistance is essential to save lives. However, it is not the solution" ; "Real solutions are, above all, political and require targeted, sustainable actions to address the root causes of the conflicts."

a2118.speaker: Humanitarian partners in the DRC
a2118.speech: Said the response this year aims to meet the most urgent needs and alleviate suffering through swift and effective assistance, adapted to the conditions on the ground ; called on the Congolese Government, the international community, and national and international humanitarian partners for a collective surge of solidarity to implement the plan with the necessary resources, access, and support.

a2118.speaker: United States government (Washington)
a2118.speech: Announced in January that it was freezing all foreign aid payments for at least 90 days.

a2345.speaker: Atunlo worker (anonymous)
a2345.speech: "There are no means, not even to buy food. I have difficulty doing many things I used to do" ; "Here, the situation is getting worse and worse, because they are not paying us", adding that even so the company asks them to carry out some tasks on the premises ; "As they are not paying, I no longer have money to take food to work" ; "The end of the month comes and they say nothing. The agreement was to pay us half of that amount and now they are dividing it, they pay only 3,500 escudos" ; "I am not going to keep waiting for them" ; "I have a contract [with Atunlo] and cannot sign with another company", but "I cannot go to work, to please them, and continue to go hungry", saying the dilemma is common to other colleagues.

a2345.speaker: Another Atunlo worker (anonymous)
a2345.speech: Said he has been trying to "survive" since February, that he has given up fighting for the rights linked to his employment contract and has terminated his contract with the company, which he said asked him to work but without paying a salary ; "They want us to work, but there is no money. I no longer expect anything. They give no green light, no decision, I do not think they will open."

a2345.speaker: Unions and labour authorities contacted by Lusa
a2345.speech: Gave no information on how many of the 210 workers remain tied to the company or, giving up seniority rights, preferred to look for other jobs.

a2345.speaker: Heidi Ganeto, coordinator of the Union of General Industry, Food, Construction and Services (Siacsa)
a2345.speech: Confirmed to Lusa the irregularities in payments to workers, saying the situation has already been reported to the General Labour Inspectorate ; "Of course the union sees this as very hard for the workers, but unfortunately everything falls within Article 198 of the labour code, we can do nothing."

a2345.speaker: Article 198 of the Cabo Verde labour code (legal text)
a2345.speech: Provides that an employer may "suspend the work of all or some workers for up to 120 days on the grounds of cyclical difficulties" or others, and that the maximum duration of the suspension may be adjusted by agreement between the parties.

a2345.speaker: Atunlo and the General Labour Inspectorate
a2345.speech: Lusa tried to obtain additional information from Atunlo and the General Labour Inspectorate, but without results.

a2345.speaker: José Manuel Albares, Spanish Minister of Foreign Affairs
a2345.speech: "We addressed [the matter] in a broad context, that of economic development and Spanish investment, which is beneficial for both countries. There is great interest from our companies" ; "Sometimes specific situations arise that have to be resolved and, of course, the Government of Cabo Verde has the best will to do so", he added without further details.

a2390.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a2390.speech: “This summit is focused on action; what matters is the megawatts produced.” He added: “Collaboration between heads of state, the private sector, development banks and civil society is essential.”

a2390.speaker: Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP)
a2390.speech: Announced an initial contribution of 10 million dollars to support 11 countries.

a2390.speaker: Dar es Salaam Declaration (summit declaration)
a2390.speech: Highlights five strategic areas: producing low-cost electricity by increasing national capacity, strengthening regional integration through interconnected grids, expanding access to electricity with particular attention to rural areas, encouraging private investment by creating a favourable framework, and improving the efficiency of public utilities.

a2390.speaker: Wale Edun, Nigerian Minister of the Economy
a2390.speech: Underlined that Nigeria illustrates the potential of these priorities, with 150 mini-grids and one million stand-alone solar connections already in place.

a2390.speaker: Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, Ivorian Minister of Energy
a2390.speech: Underlined the importance of regional electricity trade; indicated that Côte d’Ivoire trades with six countries and plans to double exports by 2030, before pointing out that payments remain a challenge.

a2390.speaker: Situmbeko Musokotwane, Zambian Minister of Finance
a2390.speech: Insisted on the urgency of increasing energy production to accompany the expected tripling of copper production over the next ten years.

a2390.speaker: Daniel Schroth, Director of Renewable Energy at the African Development Bank
a2390.speech: Recalled that every delay worsens inequalities. “This initiative is a historic opportunity for Africa,” he insisted.

a2460.speaker: Ahmed Kedir, distribution and fleet management director at the Ethiopian Pharmaceuticals Supply Agency
a2460.speech: "We're working hard to provide the insecticide nets before the rainy season arrives in the areas where malaria outbreak is anticipated."

a2460.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a2460.speech: The Ministry of Health estimates that there are about 12 million suspected cases of malaria in the country every year.

a2460.speaker: Henok Zewdu (MD), lecturer at Debre Tabor University College of Medicine and Health Science
