a2460.speech: Appreciates the early distribution of the nets, saying that it indicates the level of precaution being taken by the government ; The distribution of the nets has to be accompanied with instructions on how to use them effectively and keep them safe for the intended period, according to Henok ; "Parallel to the distribution of the insecticide nets, draining places with stagnant water and giving a memorable lesson to the entire community are the basic measures that reduce the spread of the disease."

a2704.speaker: Anthony G. Myers, Liberia's Deputy Finance Minister for Fiscal Affairs
a2704.speech: Emphasized the critical link between financial autonomy and effective decentralization, noting that Liberia's development agenda hinges on empowering local governments with both authority and resources. "Administrative decentralization without fiscal empowerment is performative," he cautioned, adding that President Joseph Boakai has consistently championed decentralization as a national priority.

a2704.speaker: Anthony G. Myers, Liberia's Deputy Finance Minister for Fiscal Affairs
a2704.speech: Highlighted the readiness of central institutions such as the Liberia Revenue Authority and the Internal Audit Agency, while underscoring the urgent need to replicate such capacity at the county level ; Encouraged participants to become trainers upon return, signaling the start of a broader national rollout ; Described the initiative as a "strategic step" toward institutional reform, framing the training as part of Liberia's commitment to South-South cooperation and sustainable public financial management.

a2704.speaker: Professor P.O. Olapegba, Vice Chancellor of the University of Ibadan
a2704.speech: Urged African nations to reduce dependency on foreign aid and stem the tide of youth emigration, criticizing what he called a "begging culture" among African leaders. "There is no free lunch - even in Freetown," he said, warning that reliance on aid undermines sovereignty and policy autonomy. He challenged African governments to build robust systems that retain local talent and questioned the applicability of Western training to African realities: "Harvard and Oxford won't solve African problems - we must."

a2831.speaker: Donald Trump's inner circle / entourage
a2831.speech: openly criticised Joe Biden's decision to authorise Ukraine to strike Russian territory with American-made long-range missiles, calling it an "escalation" and a threat of a "third world war" ; accused Joe Biden of risking an escalation "for political ends."

a2831.speaker: The Kremlin
a2831.speech: promised an "appropriate" response if these ATACMS missiles are fired at Russia.

a2831.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a2831.speech: had warned that such a decision would mean that "the NATO countries are at war with Russia."

a2831.speaker: The New York Times, citing American officials speaking on condition of anonymity
a2831.speech: reports that the ATACMS missiles supplied by the United States should be used in the Russian border region of Kursk, where North Korean soldiers have been deployed in support of Russian troops, and that Washington's decision to allow Ukraine to use these missiles came in reaction to this deployment of North Korean troops.

a2831.speaker: Richard Grenell, former US Director of National Intelligence (2017-2021)
a2831.speech: wrote on X: "No one anticipated that Joe Biden would be responsible for escalating the war in Ukraine during the transition period. It is as if he were launching a whole new war."

a2831.speaker: Mike Waltz, Florida Representative and incoming National Security Adviser to Donald Trump
a2831.speech: said on Fox: "This is a new step in the escalation and no one knows where it will lead us."

a2831.speaker: Mike Waltz, Florida Representative and incoming National Security Adviser to Donald Trump
a2831.speech: said: "How do you bring both parties to the negotiating table to end this war? What is the framework of a deal and who sits at that table? These are the questions that President Trump and I are going to work on."

a2831.speaker: Donald Trump Jr., son of the former president
a2831.speech: added on X: "The military-industrial complex that seems to want to make sure it triggers the third world war before my father has the chance to establish peace and save lives."

a2831.speaker: Steven Cheung, spokesman for Donald Trump's campaign team
a2831.speech: indicated that Donald Trump was "the only one able to bring both parties to negotiate peace and to work to end the war and the killing."

a2831.speaker: Matthew Miller, US State Department spokesman
a2831.speech: replied at his daily briefing that Russia alone was responsible for a "major escalation" by having accepted the deployment on its soil of thousands of North Korean soldiers, and that there was "only one president at a time."

a2831.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a2831.speech: welcomed the American announcement with caution, merely noting that these weapons "will speak for themselves."

a2831.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a2831.speech: promised to end the war in "24 hours" - without revealing how - and has questioned the tens of billions of dollars spent (more than 60 billion) by Washington in favour of Ukraine since the Russian invasion.

a3049.speaker: Innocent Shiyo, Permanent Representative of Tanzania to the AU and Ambassador to Ethiopia
a3049.speech: issued a communique, saying that the Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation, Ambassador Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, ably represented President Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan ; said that participation of Tanzania in this strategic convening was in its capacity as the Third Vice Chairperson of the Bureau of the Assembly of the African Union for the year 2025 ; noted that Tanzania's presence underscored its unwavering commitment to the African integration agenda and its enduring resolve to advance the principles of unity, solidarity, shared prosperity, and sustainable development on the continent.

a3049.speaker: Innocent Shiyo, Permanent Representative of Tanzania to the AU and Ambassador to Ethiopia
a3049.speech: noted that the Meeting was attended by 13 Heads of State and Government, comprising five members of the AU Bureau and eight chairpersons of the RECs, alongside other high-ranking dignitaries ; said that the meeting received and considered a series of comprehensive and policy-rich reports, including: the Status of Continental Integration in Africa; Reports from the Chairpersons of RECs and RMs; the Role of AUDA-NEPAD in advancing regional and continental integration; the Status of Implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

a3049.speaker: Joao Lourenco, President of the Republic of Angola and Chairperson of the African Union
a3049.speech: told members it was time to reflect on the African regional integration process and its present state, taking into account the fulfillment of the fundamental objectives and goals of the Agenda 2063, 'The Africa We Want'. "We express our highest gratitude to His Excellency President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo and the people of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea for agreeing to host this important Summit and for the warm welcome and exceptional hospitality reserved for all delegations since our arrival in the beautiful and welcoming city of Malabo. As we all know and defend, regional integration in Africa is more than an ideal it is, above all, one of the essential vectors for transforming the great ambitions of the Agenda 2063 into concrete progress and a profoundly strategic necessity for the African continent, marked by borders inherited from the colonial era, which have often ignored the cultural, social and economic realities of the African people. It is precisely in this context that the need arises to strengthen coordination between our continental organization and the Regional Economic Communities and Regional Mechanisms, on the understanding that the latter are the essential pillars of the African architecture. Africa, as driver for interconnecting continental policies and national dynamics in the most varied fields."

a3049.speaker: African Union Commission (report on the Status of Continental Integration)
a3049.speech: presented a meticulously detailed report on the Status of Continental Integration, structured around four foundational pillars: political integration, economic integration, infrastructure development, and human and social development. While acknowledging significant progress made by RECs such as the EAC, COMESA, ECOWAS and SADC, the report emphasized the persistent challenges impeding deeper integration. These include the slow pace of ratification of legal instruments, the absence of harmonised statistical frameworks, fragmented implementation approaches, and the undue influence of external actors undermining Africa's self-defined priorities.

a3049.speaker: The Seventh Mid-Year Coordination Meeting
a3049.speech: called upon all stakeholders to reaffirm their commitment to the Pan-African ideal by accelerating the ratification and implementation of key legal instruments, prioritising investments in human capital, reinforcing institutional coordination among AU organs and RECs, advancing the digital transformation agenda, and mobilising domestic and innovative sources of financing to ensure long-term sustainability of integration initiatives ; endorsed the proposal to establish the African Union Agenda 2063 Development Fund, with four strategic financing windows dedicated to infrastructure and transport, industrial and trade development, human capital development, and institutional governance and regulatory reform ; called for intensified efforts to address structural constraints, particularly those affecting small and medium enterprises, informal trade, and the operationalisation of key flagship initiatives including SAATM, the African Union Financial Institutions, the Single African Passport, and the Free Movement of Persons Protocol ; endorsed the Joint Resource Mobilisation Strategy and urged accelerated implementation in support of the AU Master Roadmap on Silencing the Guns and Agenda 2063.

a3049.speaker: Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President of the Arab Republic of Egypt and Chairperson of the Heads of State and Government Orientation Committee (HSGOC) (AUDA-NEPAD presentation/report)
a3049.speech: The report underlined the imperative of establishing a sustainable continental development fund to finance the implementation of Agenda 2063, noting that over USD 3.3 trillion will be required.

a3049.speaker: Issoufou Mahamadou, AfCFTA Champion and former President of Niger
a3049.speech: gave an authoritative update on the African Continental Free Trade Area: as of July 2025, 49 out of the 54 signatory States had deposited their instruments of ratification, with Eritrea remaining the only country yet to sign the Agreement.

a3049.speaker: Southern African Development Community (SADC) report on geopolitical trends
a3049.speech: presented a sober yet forward-looking analysis of the external environment. The report cautioned against the resurgence of trade protectionism, reductions in official development assistance, and macroeconomic instability.

a3094.speaker: USAID's implementing partners
a3094.speech: Have reiterated calls for an end to violence against women and girls in South Sudan, as the country marks 16 Days of Activism against Gender Based Violence; speaking on Eye Radio's Dawn Show on November 25, the U.S. agency's implementing partners said women and girls should be protected and respected in the country.

a3094.speaker: World Health Organization
a3094.speech: According to the World Health Organization, globally, one in three women experience either intimate partner violence or non-partner sexual violence during their lifetime.

a3094.speaker: Boboya James, senior technical advisor with Sustainable Independent Media Activity (SIMA)
a3094.speech: Called for collective efforts to end GBV in South Sudan ; "We need to continue to promote the women voice in South Sudan" ; "We need to continue to build leadership around women-like initiatives, and we should continue to support initiatives like the media, where you produce a lot of content and begin to increase talks, outreach, roundtable discussion of these topics" ; said there should be dialogue with government officials to engage them in taking up their responsibilities of implementing some of the laws and policies ; "Awareness in community level is very important, a lot of funding is going to local organizations to be able to capitalize on this GBV related issues in the communities."

a3094.speaker: Gloria George, Gender Based Violence Officer with UNICEF
a3094.speech: Says for GBV to end in the country, there is need for collective efforts ; "One hand cannot do it, so everybody needs to come on board and we see how this GBV really comes to an end" ; "We have to create an environment that women and girls, even men and boys are able to move freely, are able to interact, are able to say what is in their mind and have the positive change that we need."

a3094.speaker: Caroline Hlatywayo, gender specialist of the Resilience through Agriculture Activity (RASS)
a3094.speech: Said communities need to be empowered to do away with cases of GBV in the country ; "Let us work on strengthening local capacity and community engagement. We need to empower communities to identify and address the root causes of GBV and leverage their inside into social, cultural and economic factor."

a3094.speaker: Museme Munira, USAID's Gender Specialist
a3094.speech: Said realizing the importance of working together and collaborating across different institutions, stakeholders, development partners and women and girls is key to winning the war on GBV ; "This is something that affects all of us, and for many nations that have moved ahead in dealing with issues of reducing GBV and focusing on empowering all sections of society have had very great progress. We would like to see that in South Sudan that we have progress."

a3134.speaker: A member of the US Congress (unnamed)
a3134.speech: Declared that USAID was financing terrorism in Africa.

a3134.speaker: Sergey Lavrov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
a3134.speech: Declared that Russia is opening seven new embassies in Africa.

a3242.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti
a3242.speech: Thanked President Samia Suluhu and Tanzania for the exceptional welcome in Dar es Salaam and said: "Our collective presence in this place, united by a common cause, illustrates our convergent vision for the future of the African continent" ; said the summit comes at a historic moment and that "Africa's energy autonomy cannot remain a mere aspiration - it constitutes an immediate imperative," adding that declarations alone are not enough and that every State, every development partner and every private sector actor must combine efforts to accelerate Africa's energy transformation.

a3242.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti
a3242.speech: Said the Republic of Djibouti has taken a resolute decision and made the energy question an absolute national priority, because no other path could lead to its ambition of an emerging and transformed Djibouti, the nation's energy supply being a sine qua non condition ; said Djibouti has instituted major structural reforms, established public-private partnerships, liberalised its electricity market to independent producers and put in place a rigorous regulatory framework; that the Goubet wind complex produces sixty megawatts, that construction of a first solar plant at Grand Bara will shortly be inaugurated with a capacity of twenty-five megawatts, and that thanks to hydroelectric imports from Ethiopia combined with the wind farm 85% of Djibouti's energy supply now comes from renewable sources, with geothermal, tidal and biomass projects under development.

a3242.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti
a3242.speech: Raised "without detour" the reality that the industrialised nations built their prosperity on the unrestricted exploitation of their natural resources and that some still derive considerable benefits from it; said the assumption that Africa should assume responsibility for their industrial excesses "is not merely inequitable - it is morally unacceptable" ; affirmed Africa's legitimate right to development in accordance with global climate imperatives, saying this is "not only an energy question - it is a question of fundamental fairness."

a3242.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti
a3242.speech: Said what hinders African progress "is not our capacity - it is global governance," with States taking on considerable debt to implement climate-resilient energy strategies while the financial support promised by the international community "remains largely theoretical" ; gave his unwavering support to Mission 300 and welcomed the recent establishment of the African Private Sector Assistance Fund, praising the African Union, the World Bank, the African Development Bank and technical and financial partners ; called for freeing Africa "from the shackles of unequal exchange" and for an international economic order that serves all nations, concluding that transformation requires enlightened political decisions, constructive dialogue and unshakeable solidarity: "The power of transformation is in our hands. The responsibility falls fully upon us. The time has come for us to act!"

a3250.speaker: Edouard Sehlin, Director General of the SME Development Agency (ADPME), Benin
a3250.speech: According to him, ADPME is tasked with informing, advising, supervising and steering micro, small and medium-sized enterprises toward existing support mechanisms, supporting their categorization, helping them seize opportunities and backing high-potential firms: "This may involve capacity building, advice, diagnostics or networking, and facilitating access to financing." ; He explains that in terms of financing the Agency plays a catalytic role in order to encourage financial actors to intervene in market segments, or categories of enterprises, in which they are not sufficiently present.

a3250.speaker: Edouard Sehlin, Director General of the SME Development Agency (ADPME), Benin
a3250.speech: "All the projects planned in the SME sector have been finalized and are starting up with all the partners. We will do more, because this makes it possible to have an impact and to have a critical mass of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises capable of contributing to the structural transformation of the economy and ensuring Benin's prosperity in the future..."

a3250.speaker: Modeste Tihounte Kerekou, Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion, Benin
a3250.speech: Said the PAG 2016-2021 amounted to around 9,038 billion CFA francs, with the intention of generating 500,000 direct and indirect jobs, and that the bar had been passed: "We were already at more than 600,000 direct and indirect jobs more than a year before the end of the five-year term. The PAG 2021-2026 is 12,011 billion CFA francs and 1,300,000 jobs that the government intends to create in close cooperation with the private sector. That is why a good part of the reforms completed in the first term have continued, and their effects are increasingly visible." ; He cites in particular the facilitation of business creation as well as the entire legislative framework put in place through the investment code, the law on the promotion of SMEs, and the law on hiring procedures in the Republic of Benin.

a3250.speaker: Modeste Tihounte Kerekou, Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion, Benin
a3250.speech: "We have an organization of the crafts world that has been completely overhauled so that it complies not only with the law, but also with the provisions of the WAEMU community code." ; He adds that in place of the old structure a chamber of trades has been enshrined in law, endowed with a Consular Assembly made up of 80 members elected by their peers, drawn from 164 trades in accordance with the WAEMU nomenclature of craft trades, namely 40 trade bodies and eight branches of activity.

a3250.speaker: Urbain Amegbedji, Director General of the National Employment Agency (ANPE), Benin
a3250.speech: "The government has made available to us new tools that make it possible to promote employment more effectively and efficiently, in particular the Special Employment Integration Programme (PSIE), which has been in effect since 2020, and which today makes it possible to impact around 3,000 young people who work in companies and whose salaries and all charges are covered by the State." ; He assures that through the PSIE there is support both for the company and for the professional integration of young people, with much greater effectiveness than in the past, and explains that the youth inclusion project makes it possible, in an average of 6 months, to train and put to work a young person who can immediately obtain a contract and start working.

a3250.speaker: Robert N'Dah Sinkeni, Director of Crafts, Benin
a3250.speech: "The Chamber of Trades and Crafts has as its essential mission to represent the sector before the public authorities and any other body, to defend the interests of artisans, and to work for the promotion of the sector."

a3328.speaker: Ato Zemen Junedi, Investment Promotion and Marketing Executive of the Industrial Parks Development Corporation
a3328.speech: Said that more than 80 different investments had been attracted to the special economic zones administered by the Corporation ; further stated that, of the total investment attracted, the investors are Chinese, Russian, Vietnamese and domestic, and that they will operate in pharmaceuticals, agro-processing - particularly coffee and tea - electric vehicle assembly, and other technology and manufacturing sectors.

a3328.speaker: Industrial Parks Development Corporation (six-month performance report)
a3328.speech: Noted that, through the investments attracted, 14 production sheds and more than 70 hectares of developed land were transferred to the investors; it was stated that over the past six months investors registering more than 597 million US dollars in investment had entered the special economic zones and the Dire Dawa free trade zone.

a3328.speaker: Industrial Parks Development Corporation (corporate data)
a3328.speech: Indicates that the investments will be located in Mekelle, Bole Lemi, Kilinto, Kombolcha, the Dire Dawa special free trade zone, and the Jimma and Semera special economic zones.

a3385.speaker: Vetaruhe Kandorozu, National Unity Democratic Organisation (Nudo) parliamentarian
a3385.speech: Said it is the government's responsibility to make sure that its citizens are educated; in his contribution to the 2025/26 budget of N$24.8 billion allocated to the education ministry in the National Assembly, he questioned why the government is "selling education" to its citizens ; "The government must ensure that all its inhabitants are well-educated and ready to contribute to the social welfare and economic development of the country. This government pressures parents to pay for school, hostel and stationery. But it must be its responsibility to ensure that free access to education is implemented and encouraged among all citizens," he said ; proposed free primary, secondary and tertiary education to enable all citizens to complete their studies without hindrance ; "Those at tertiary institutions must receive a monthly fee of N$1 500 for the period of their studies. No registration and tuition fees must be paid in Namibia," he said.

a3385.speaker: Vetaruhe Kandorozu, National Unity Democratic Organisation (Nudo) parliamentarian
a3385.speech: Added that there is no emphasis given on technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and proposed the establishment of vocational training centres in each region, and up to the constituency level ; "The TVET programmes must be introduced from primary up to secondary schools as an exit point to the vocational centres," said the MP.

a3385.speaker: Vetaruhe Kandorozu, National Unity Democratic Organisation (Nudo) parliamentarian
a3385.speech: Added that the government has "entered the business of exporting money", paying high interest rates on foreign loans by buying all imported goods ; "This current regime cannot do any single thing within their own country - even a toothpick is imported. This budget does not talk on how to assist the youth to be self-reliant and own business," he said.

a3385.speaker: Vetaruhe Kandorozu, National Unity Democratic Organisation (Nudo) parliamentarian
a3385.speech: Called for strict rules to "stop people from Bangladesh from owning mobile phone shops made of containers that are scattered all over Namibia"; said this type of business must be owned by Namibian youth, proposing for the government to one day do away with China town and call it Namibians' town ; "Look at the Ramatex buildings - this government has no idea what to do with those buildings, rather than turning them into boxing rings, music arenas and breeding stations for cats, dogs and birds," he said.

a3471.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3471.speech: Says it is devising strategies to cushion the economy from the impact of the temporary ban on foreign aid imposed by United States of America President Donald Trump.

a3471.speaker: Foreign assistance portal on the United States Agency for International Development (USAid) website (data)
a3471.speech: Trump's order on aid put on hold $284.7 million (about K493.7 billion) financing to Malawi, according to data published on the foreign assistance portal on the USAid website.

a3471.speaker: Boston Maliketi Banda, Reserve Bank of Malawi spokesperson
a3471.speech: In a written response yesterday, said the temporary ban on foreign aid is a concern for many developing countries which are ordinarily strategising on how to overcome the shock ; said such policy shifts in traditional donor countries like the US are driven by the need to better the lives of their citizenry, as per the ambitions of any administration ; “This is one of the reasons the governor [of RBM] has embarked on an engagement drive with key stakeholders, including the media to collaboratively develop practical and implementable strategies to address such shocks and sustainably address the forex supply shortages in the country,” said Maliketi Banda.

a3471.speaker: Boston Maliketi Banda, Reserve Bank of Malawi spokesperson
a3471.speech: Said RBM has welcomed and is promoting the use of plastic money for both domestic and cross-border payments, and that the use of plastic money such as credit and debit cards can contribute to a decrease in the supply of physical dollar notes on the parallel market.

a3471.speaker: Money market experts (Monetary Policy Technical Committee Forum in Blantyre)
a3471.speech: Suggested the promotion of plastic money for domestic and cross-border payments during a Monetary Policy Technical Committee Forum in Blantyre.

a3471.speaker: Economists
a3471.speech: Last month, economists expressed fears that the temporary ban on aid could worsen the forex shortages the country is experiencing in the short to medium term.

a3471.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) data
a3471.speech: RBM data show that forex reserves in November 2024 had dropped to $516.9 million or 2.1 months of import cover, far below the 3.9 months of import cover recommended by multilateral institutions such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

a3583.speaker: Economists surveyed by Reuters
a3583.speech: The median forecast among economists surveyed by Reuters was for the inflation rate to reach 3.3%.

a3583.speaker: Lesetja Kganyago, Governor of the South African Reserve Bank
a3583.speech: has warned that the global environment is concerning.

a3583.speaker: Many economists
a3583.speech: still forecast at least one rate reduction this year, while the markets are not expecting more cuts.

a3619.speaker: Honey Malinga, Director of Petroleum at Uganda’s Energy Ministry
a3619.speech: Told URN that the Final Investment Decision had what he described as a “trigger effect” leading to a beehive of activities in the Tilenga and Kingfisher areas: “The final investment decision was a key achievement for the three projects. From EACOP, Tilenga, and the Kingfisher. So we started on a good note though in September we had issues with the EU resolution. But generally, the year has been good for the industry.”

a3619.speaker: Honey Malinga, Director of Petroleum at Uganda’s Energy Ministry
a3619.speech: Told URN that while no objection had been received from the public on the EACOP construction permit, the ministry was in final stages of the exercise to ensure compliance with Environmental, Social, and Governance requirements: “The law says 106 days. So we expect a decision late this month or early next year. Because I think there are some conditions that they never fulfilled at the beginning. They were supposed to make the application with payment but they didn’t.”

a3619.speaker: Honey Malinga, Director of Petroleum at Uganda’s Energy Ministry
a3619.speech: Revealed, on the stalled second licensing round: “The Minister has to let the cabinet know about the process before we sign. So we have two companies waiting for us to get a green light from the cabinet before we can award the licenses.”

a3619.speaker: Ernest Rubondo, Executive Director of the Petroleum Authority of Uganda (PAU)
a3619.speech: Told journalists earlier this year that 2022 was going to commence the period of three years of intense infrastructure development in preparation for the first oil in 2025, and predicted that investments in the sector were likely to shoot to $3 billion compared to $230 million in 2019, $180 million in 2020, and $500 million in 2021: “Ugandans need to get excited and prepare for what is coming ahead, and the transformation it is already bringing.” He also suggested that 40% of the $15-20 billion to be invested during the development phase will be retained through national content.

a3619.speaker: Ernest Rubondo, Executive Director of the Petroleum Authority of Uganda (PAU)
a3619.speech: On Uganda’s petroleum resources: “These resources, much as they look very small compared to the large producers, are a very good beginning for the country. Because they will enable the production of 200,000 barrels of crude oil per day for the country. And it is important to note that these resources are in only 15% of Albertine Graben which is currently licensed.” According to Rubondo, there is potential for more oil to be discovered in 2023 from the ongoing exploration being undertaken by Oranto Petroleum and Australia’s Armour Energy in the Ngasa and Kanywataba contracts.

a3619.speaker: Emmanuel Mugarura, CEO of the Association of Uganda Oil and Gas Service Providers (AUGOS)
a3619.speech: Said a number of Ugandan suppliers were already partaking of part of that pie: “Yes, people are getting money. Unfortunately, most of the money is not being kept here. Most of the money is going to other countries. Why? I don’t know outside countries. But mainly because other people seem to be more prepared than we are.”

a3619.speaker: Economic Policy Research Centre (EPRC) researchers (study)
a3619.speech: Researchers working on a study to identify linkages between the agriculture sector and the oil and gas sector found in July that the influx of people in the Albertine region had led to a shortage of supply of meat, vegetables, and milk in the Albertine.

a3619.speaker: Moses Odonkonyero, EPRC research lead
a3619.speech: Explained: “If you consider the core oil districts and spillover districts, you find that the rate at which demand is growing is faster in the core districts than the spillover districts.”

a3619.speaker: Sources (anonymous, including a source at TotalEnergies) speaking to URN
a3619.speech: Told URN that about 90% of the work had been completed by Mota-Engil Uganda as the year ends; a source at TotalEnergies told URN the contracted companies were in the advanced stages of the work; sources indicated that the change of the December 20 drilling flag-off date at Kingfisher was due to pending work on the waste management facility for drill cuttings; and sources told URN that while Luwero Industries has already been established on the ground with a camp to house 150 people, the facility still had some issues related to the power supply.

a3619.speaker: Penina Aheebwa, PAU Director of Support Services
a3619.speech: Defended EACOP in September, saying those fighting its development were against the development of Uganda: “They should be aware of the value of over US$ 81 billion (almost double Uganda’s current GDP) at stake from Uganda’s oil and gas projects. Additionally, the perceived environmental impacts have been fully addressed through the established of Environmental and Social assessment (ESIA) processes to the highest international standards,” said Aheebwa in a statement.

a3619.speaker: Prof Benedict Oramah, Afreximbank chairman, and his executive team
a3619.speech: Said in October that financing EACOP and the refinery in Uganda was a strategic business that will uplift African economies’ armory to fight poverty.

a3619.speaker: State House of Uganda (reports)
a3619.speech: Reported at the end of the US-Africa Leaders’ summit that the Albertine Graben Refinery Consortium (AGRC) has reached an agreement on capital investments.

a3810.speaker: Mozambican Ministry of Economy and Finance (press release)
a3810.speech: said that, with the signature of the revised CDF agreement, 10.75 million dollars will be allocated to the preparation of Compact II, which is expected to benefit the entire country, but with a geographical emphasis on the central province of Zambezia.

a3810.speaker: Max Tonela, Mozambican Minister of Economy and Finance
a3810.speech: said his signature represents an important commitment leading towards the qualitative design of Compact II, and that the compact will contain projects in areas such as the promotion of investments in commercial agriculture; rural connectivity and transport; and the integrated management of climate and coastal development ; “I would like to reiterate the commitment of the Mozambican government to strengthen the capacity of our institutions to implement solid economic policies and fiscal reforms, which will improve the cornerstones of the social and economic development of Mozambique.”

a3810.speaker: Fatema Z. Sumar, MCC Deputy President for Compact Operations
a3810.speech: “We are pleased to take the next step in our partnership with the Mozambican government” ; “The signing of the Revised Agreement on the Compact Development Fund will continue to mark progress towards a successful MCC Mozambique Compact” ; “With the funding that will be made available, the MCC and the Mozambican government will work to identify investment projects to reduce poverty and to speed up inclusive and sustainable economic growth.”

a3937.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a3937.speech: Underscored significant advancements in health, education, and economic sectors, affirming that the country is poised for further progress; reflected on the partnership’s achievements and expressed optimism for the future, envisioning continued progress and stronger ties between the two nations. “We also celebrate the lasting impact of innovations on development, the importance of Mozambicans in leadership, and a future full of potential. We have been with Mozambique over the years and will continue to work alongside the Mozambican people, building a more prosperous, healthier and inclusive future for all.”

a3937.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID Mission Director in Mozambique
a3937.speech: Stressed that Mozambique’s experience shows that development is about harmonizing efforts and collaboration.

a4230.speaker: Government of Mali
a4230.speech: “Welcomes” the abolition of USAID funding for “social cohesion” and similar programmes in the Sahel region at the initiative of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), and even calls for individuals to be punished.

a4230.speaker: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a4230.speech: “Furthermore, the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs calls on the American authorities to institute proceedings against the persons who diverted these funds to finance the international terrorism of which Mali and other States of the Confederation of Sahel States are victims.”

a4230.speaker: Malian authorities
a4230.speech: Believe that these funds support terrorism.

a4230.speaker: Elon Musk
a4230.speech: Apparently shares the view of the authorities of sovereign Mali, since he relayed on Twitter the statement of the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (see screenshot).

a4261.speaker: Marie Darrieussecq, writer
a4261.speech: "The world is a Norwegian ship full of Afghan refugees stranded off the coast of Australia."

a4261.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (data/report)
a4261.speech: According to recent IOM data, more than 4.5 million people were forced to flee their homes in the Sahel in 2024.

a4261.speaker: IOM figures corroborated by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4261.speech: Reveal that many displacement camps host on average between 10,000 and 20,000 people, with some sites reaching critical levels of overcrowding.

a4261.speaker: Joint reports of OCHA and the World Bank
a4261.speech: Set out a worrying reality regarding sanitary conditions in the camps: nearly 70% of these facilities face major difficulties in access to drinking water and waste management, failings that represent a major health risk for already fragile populations.

a4261.speaker: Solidarité Internationale (humanitarian organisation)
a4261.speech: Points to an unequal distribution of food supplies, making food insecurity chronic.

a4261.speaker: The World Bank and OCHA
a4261.speech: Call for reinforced support measures to remedy the shortcomings in sanitation infrastructure.

a4261.speaker: Solidarité Internationale (humanitarian organisation)
a4261.speech: Is campaigning for a reallocation of climate and humanitarian financing in order to adapt responses to the specific needs of displaced communities.

a4261.speaker: Recent reports of the IOM, OCHA, the World Bank and Solidarité Internationale
a4261.speech: Insist on the need to invest in resilient infrastructure capable of withstanding growing demographic pressure, so as to guarantee continuous access to essential services even in a context of chronic instability.

a4342.speaker: Abida Mia, Malawi's Minister of Water and Sanitation
a4342.speech: Urged the tea sector to embrace value-addition for the country to reap more benefits: "While we take pride in Malawi's rich tea history, the future demands that we evolve. It is time to focus on value-addition - moving beyond simply producing raw tea and investing in processes such as blending, packaging, and branding within Malawi itself." ; called for collaboration among tea sector players to propel Malawi tea onto the global stage: "Together we can invest in both branding and value-added processes that can propel Malawian tea onto the global stage."

a4342.speaker: Sangwani Hara, Tea Association of Malawi chairperson
a4342.speech: Said his association believes that trade pacts and enhanced trade can provide a good alternative to aid and development assistance: "With increased tea imports from Malawi, British tea drinkers will be allowed to consume a great product at a fair price while contributing to Malawi's and tea estates' foreign exchange earnings and development agenda."

a4342.speaker: Thomas Bisika, Malawi High Commissioner
a4342.speech: Said tea will play a significant role as Malawi transitions from aid to trade; thanked Sureena Brackenridge, MP, and Warinder Juss, MP, for hosting the event.

a4342.speaker: Sheikh Aliur Rahman, London Tea Exchange chief executive officer
a4342.speech: Called for fair play in the tea production chain.

a4379.speaker: Anthony Kasunda, presidential press secretary
a4379.speech: According to Kasunda, the two ministers briefed the President on “measures being taken” to investigate the violence, following Chakwera’s earlier directive while in Nigeria.

a4379.speaker: Human rights advocates and political analysts
a4379.speech: Say the President’s move is cosmetic and reactionary—falling far short of the decisive action Malawians expected.

a4379.speaker: Wonderful Mkhutche, political analyst
a4379.speech: “What is there to investigate when the attackers were caught on camera?” asked Mkhutche ; “If the government was serious, arrests would have already been made.”

a4379.speaker: Robert Mkwezalamba, Human Rights Consultative Committee chairperson
a4379.speech: Slammed the delay as a dangerous signal of tolerance for impunity ; “The President should have fired the Inspector General and army commander by now. That would show he means business,” he said.

a4379.speaker: Mabvuto Bamusi, Political Science Association
a4379.speech: Went further, calling the presidency’s response “a disappointing cover-up” and a “victory for the panga-wielding thugs.”

a4379.speaker: Local and international bodies, including the European Union
a4379.speech: Condemned the violence and threatened aid cuts.

a4379.speaker: Police (Malawi)
a4379.speech: Claim investigations are still ongoing—despite clear video evidence and eyewitness accounts.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said the key purpose of his visit was to convey the continued support and continued commitment of the entire UN family to South Sudan, especially as it enters the fourth extension of its transitional period amidst a variety of challenges: “So, the commitment is fully there, both by UNMISS as well as by the UN agencies” ; said it was critical to emphasize that UN commitment when the country is doing its best to fully implement the Revitalized Peace Agreement and hold its first elections, due by December 2026 ; assured interlocutors of Secretary-General António Guterres' strong commitment to continue supporting South Sudan and making sure attention will not be diverted from the South Sudanese situation.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said he is aware of serious challenges faced by the South Sudanese people and their leaders - the dire economic and humanitarian situation, rising insecurity at the subnational level and currents of violence in various parts of the country, and the impact of the Sudanese conflict in terms of IDPs, refugees, returnees, the economy and potential security effects ; said the situation in South Sudan is part of simultaneous crises across the world which have led to considerable pressure on the international community, particularly on humanitarian funding: “Simply put – there are too many people in need and too few resources available” ; said main contributors have constraints on their public finances and that effective advocacy for the resources South Sudan needs will require the partnership of all, including the authorities of South Sudan.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Highlighted the hope that the parties to the Revitalized Agreement will break political deadlocks through consensus and move forward swiftly to ensure this latest extension leads to elections under the best possible circumstances ; said completing a peaceful democratic transition is a common goal between South Sudan and the international community, but that it is the South Sudanese themselves, and first and foremost the authorities, who must do the heavy lifting, with the UN there to assist them in every way it can.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said that on the crisis in Sudan and Abyei-related matters, including intercommunal tensions between the Ngok Dinka and Twic Dinka communities and the fallout from the conflict in Sudan on the Abyei Box, it was agreed that building trust and confidence among both communities and ensuring active dialogue between all key stakeholders is paramount, noting the final status of Abyei remains open and that regular and effective dialogue between the parties is important.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said on Sudan that the objective of the UN is to promote dialogue and a return to peace, and that the Secretary-General's envoy, Mr. [Ramtane] Lamamra, is working very hard to achieve these objectives ; said it was not the UN who decided to withdraw UNAMID but the new government of Sudan, and that when a host country decides it no longer wants a peacekeeping mission on its territory, the only thing the UN can do is withdraw ; said the lesson is that good conditions for withdrawal are where objectives have been achieved – a successful political process and strong, credible state institutions – as in Liberia, Sierra Leone, Angola, Mozambique, Cambodia and East Timor, whereas withdrawal because the host country no longer wants the mission, as in Sudan, Mali and Haiti, has altogether very different implications.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said his main message to President Kiir was the full commitment of the UN family to support South Sudan in implementing the Revitalized Agreement and preparing for elections, and that this needs an equally strong involvement and commitment from the South Sudanese authorities ; said South Sudan cannot afford another extension because the people expect elections, because of security challenges in the country and a very challenging regional environment, and because Member States, the international community, the Security Council and financial contributors to UNMISS and humanitarian assistance clearly expect progress.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said that in meetings with First Vice President Riek Machar and key signatories he heard a determination to move forward, but that a lot needs to be done, with about six specific 'low hanging fruit' actions that could be taken relatively soon on creating a favourable space for peaceful and open elections and on moving forward with the security arrangement.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said he agrees it is absolutely key to move towards building solid rule of law and security institutions, referring to how a country can transition from having a peacekeeping mission towards keeping the support of the UN in different ways.

a4560.speaker: Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations
a4560.speech: Said the UN is not in the business of recognizing governments in response to a question on a parallel government in Sudan: “What we do is we work for peace. So, it’s about bringing together stakeholders, the goodwill and the international partners that are willing to help and then working very hard to bring about an end to hostilities and [begin] constructive dialogue between them.”

a4560.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, SRSG and Head of UNMISS
a4560.speech: Said those who work in this business know there are no guarantees, that there are disappointments and slow progress, but that it has to work because 12 or 13 million people depend on the capacity of this country to organize its affairs so there is a basic level of stability ; said he is convinced the only route out of a difficult transition is through an electoral process or some process agreed by the parties, one which rewrites a social contract and sets out the platform of the national identity of the country ; noted his own country had to do exactly the same 20 years ago, and that the task would challenge even the most complex and developed societies, but “We don’t have the option of giving up.”

a4560.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, SRSG and Head of UNMISS
a4560.speech: Said disarmament remains one of the most difficult questions, that governors told him failure to disarm was most likely to lead to the failure of the project, and that the last exercise failed because a successful disarmament campaign has to have popular support and be doggedly neutral and impartial in its application ; said the country has to build its own justice chain, citing a World Bank study that countries emerging from conflict must provide jobs, provide basic safety and build institutions, and that an average rule of law institution takes 40 years to build ; said UNMISS is now putting more and more effort into the rule of law, building prisons and police stations and teaching people to read and write, and that his nightmare is leaving a country without a basic functioning police system.

a4560.speaker: Nicholas Haysom, SRSG and Head of UNMISS
a4560.speech: Said on subnational violence that “we have heard allegations that people are scared” and there is apprehension at the moment ; insisted the country must properly embark on its unification process to create a truly unified, neutral, professional and representative security apparatus better placed to engage communities and reduce violence ; said all have an obligation to advise politicians to mitigate the levels of tension, because the one thing feared is a return to war and the only thing keeping that away is the peace agreement: “If the peace agreement starts to fragment, fracture then I’m not sure what’s going to happen.”

a4560.speaker: World Bank (study)
a4560.speech: Did a study on what was required for countries emerging from conflict: “You’ve got to provide jobs. You have to provide safety – basic safety so that people can engage in rebuilding their society. And thirdly, they said you’ve got to build institutions... your average rule of law institution takes 40 years to build.” (cited by SRSG Haysom)

a4560.speaker: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and their allies (via journalist's question)
a4560.speech: Say they are going to form a parallel government in Sudan and that they might announce that [parallel] government.

a4595.speaker: Fred M'membe, Socialist Party President (Zambia)
a4595.speech: Called for urgent reforms in the country's mining sector to mitigate the economic impact of aid cuts by the United States and Switzerland; urged President Hakainde Hichilema's administration to reconsider mining tax waivers and concessions that he believes are depriving the nation of crucial revenue; and warned of the significant fiscal challenges the country was expected to face.

a4599.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (statement, quoted by Radio Mocambique)
a4599.speech: A statement from the Presidency of the Republic said the participation of the Mozambican Head of State in the conference comes in response to the invitation made jointly by the King of Jordan, Abdullah Al Hussein, the President of Egypt, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, and the Secretary General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, and that President Nyusi will be accompanied by the Minister of National Defence, Cristovao Chume, the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Manuel Goncalves, Mozambique's Ambassador to the United Nations, Pedro Comissario, and officials from the Presidency and other state institutions.

a4599.speaker: Jordanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates (@ForeignMinistry, social media post)
a4599.speech: Posted: "Now, Speech by Jordan's DPM and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Ayman Safadi @AymanHsafadi, as part of the Working Group Sessions for the Urgent Humanitarian Response for Gaza Conference, followed by speeches by Egypt's Minister of Foreign Affairs, HE Sameh Shoukry,..."

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: “The future of African agriculture will not be bankrolled by donors. It will be driven by investors” ; in a spirited interview in Nairobi on Friday, delivered a wake-up call to African governments and entrepreneurs that agriculture is Africa’s next big investment frontier.

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: “For 20 years, we’ve been urging governments to meet the 10% public investment pledge in agriculture,” referencing the Maputo and Malabo Declarations. “But the money just isn’t there. Many are drowning in debt, spending nearly half of their GDP on repayments.”

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: As traditional aid dries up — USAID has scaled back and others are following suit — AGRA is pivoting, turning the spotlight on private capital: “There’s still money out there. What’s missing is a compelling investment case” ; “We’ve spent two decades testing models that work. We know that if yields hit three metric tons per hectare, the business case is strong. Now we must speak the language of investors: ROI, scale, and resilience.”

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: “This isn’t just about maize. It’s about processing. It’s about trade. It’s about industries that create value, not just calories” ; urged governments to strengthen the capacity of banks, financial institutions, and agri-entrepreneurs to attract and deploy private capital: “We must move from subsidies to sustainability. From donor dependency to deal-making.”

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: Pointed to Mastercard’s recent multi-million-dollar investment in African agriculture — not as aid, but as business: “They’re not here for charity. They see jobs, growth, and market potential. That’s the shift we need.”

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: “You can have the best seed and science, but if the farmer doesn’t see a buyer, she won’t plant. That’s why we must build strong, reliable market systems—and that’s where private capital must come in” ; “We can’t design 21st-century food systems if we’re still excluding the people doing the actual work.”

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: Offers Malawi’s leaders both a challenge and a roadmap: “Stop waiting for aid. Start unlocking investment. Build policies that support agribusiness—from rural banks and export incentives to infrastructure.”

a4684.speaker: Alice Ruhweza, President of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a4684.speech: “We’re country-led. We’re impact-led. And we’re people-focused” ; “Africa is the youngest continent on Earth. Agriculture is its largest employer. The opportunity is staggering—if we’re bold enough to seize it.”

a4855.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a4855.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the Government of China for its continued support to Somalia, particularly in the areas of cooperation, security, economic development, and humanitarian assistance.

a4855.speaker: Wang Yu, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Somalia
a4855.speech: Underlined China's commitment to deepening its partnership with Somalia, noting the importance of expanding cooperation across key sectors that serve the mutual interests of both countries.

a5036.speaker: Maria de Fatima Manso, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Mozambican Communities
a5036.speech: Said the relationship between the Republic of Mozambique and the European Union is "comprehensive, deep and dynamic," and classified the European Union as Mozambique's largest cooperation partner in the pursuit of peace, security and development, as well as in the areas of trade, investment and humanitarian aid ; argued that this "partnership continues to be a beacon of cooperation and progress."

a5036.speaker: Maria de Fatima Manso, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Mozambican Communities
a5036.speech: Expressed the hope that the celebration would be "an opportunity for the consolidation of the strategic alignment of the AU-EU partnership, around four central pillars of the Joint Vision 2030, adopted by African and European leaders at the last summit held in Brussels, Kingdom of Belgium, in February 2022."

a5139.speaker: US government (directive)
a5139.speech: Under the latest directive of the US government, all employees of USAID are being placed on “administrative leave” and the agency will be dissolved by Friday; a letter published last Tuesday announced that USAID employees would be placed on administrative leave by the end of the week.

a5139.speaker: USAID (official notice on its website)
a5139.speech: A notice confirms that all “direct-hire personnel” are being placed on leave — with the exception of people in “mission-critical functions, core leadership roles and specially designated programmes”, who were to be notified on Thursday by USAID leadership; it further states that the agency, together with the US State Department, will organize and finance return travel for USAID employees stationed outside the USA within 30 days, with an extension considered only in individual cases, for example for family or security-related reasons. The official notice ends with: “Thank you for your service.”

a5139.speaker: Nurses in state clinics involved in the initiative (anonymous)
a5139.speech: Confirmed to the Namibian Sun that they have lost their jobs.

a5139.speaker: Affected Namibian USAID employees (anonymous)
a5139.speech: Several of those affected expressed their “disappointment, shock and hopelessness,” but did not want to disclose further details.

a5139.speaker: World Economic Forum, Global Gender Gap Report 2022
a5139.speech: According to the report, Namibia has already achieved 92:99:94 status under the UN's 95:95:95 goal for fighting HIV — a success made possible largely through PEPFAR programmes.

a5139.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Namibian Ministry of Health
a5139.speech: Had previously praised the DREAMS programme for its successes in supporting adolescent girls and young women, particularly for health counselling in dealing with HIV/AIDS.

a5139.speaker: Walters Kamaya, spokesman for the Namibian Ministry of Health
a5139.speech: Affirmed that Namibia will continue its health measures despite the loss of US aid: “With or without USAID we will continue to provide health services for our people. Of course the loss will be felt, but that cannot be an excuse to fail.” Kamaya stressed that USAID funding represents merely a supplementary resource and must also be viewed as such.

a5143.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a5143.speech: says countries across the Middle East and North Africa face significant challenges to economic growth as they face uncertainty due to tariff measures, lower-than-recent oil prices and cuts to financial aid.

a5143.speaker: IMF outlook report for the MENA region
a5143.speech: says Brent crude oil prices – which are down from highs above $120 a barrel in 2022 – are likely to be $65 to $69 per barrel in 2025 and 2026 ; adds this will make energy-exporting economies vulnerable to market fluctuations ; says that despite the global economic uncertainty, MENA nations can drive growth through structural reforms and diversifying economic ties.

a5143.speaker: Jihad Azour, IMF Director for the Middle East and Central Asia
a5143.speech: explains that tariff plans by the U.S. and other countries and geopolitical tensions have created mounting global uncertainty that could negatively impact the region’s growth by anywhere from 2% to 4.5% ; adds that reductions in foreign aid coming into the region also will play a role, especially after U.S. President Donald Trump pulled his country back from its position as the world’s single largest aid donor ; adds that although growth in the MENA region is expected to be 2.6% this year, as compared to 1.8% last year, the global economic uncertainty could impact the outlook ; urges countries in the region to “devise policies in order to protect their economies”.

a5143.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a5143.speech: says it is willing to work with some of the struggling nations and the new government in Syria.

a5143.speaker: Jihad Azour, IMF Director for the Middle East and Central Asia
a5143.speech: Speaking in Dubai, says that IMF staff and Lebanese officials are in discussions.

a5290.speaker: Office of Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre (statement on X)
a5290.speech: confirmed Hamza's Saturday meeting with Wang, where the two discussed "strengthening the deep-rooted relations and cooperation" between Somalia and China ; claimed Hamza thanked Beijing for its "multifaceted support" in politics, security, economic development, and humanitarian assistance.

a5290.speaker: Office of Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre
a5290.speech: said the Expo will focus on trade, investment, technology, and energy - areas where Somalia seeks Chinese capital.

a5290.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Somali Prime Minister
a5290.speech: once called the Jewish, "Children of pigs and monkeys."

a5290.speaker: Wang Yu, Chinese Ambassador to Somalia
a5290.speech: pledged that China would continue backing the Somali government, describing relations as "longstanding and cooperative."

a5290.speaker: Diplomatic sources in Mogadishu (anonymous)
a5290.speech: told our reporter that Wang's visit was about more than pleasantries. He not only extended the Expo invitation but also pressed Mogadishu on Beijing's growing concerns over "Somaliland's ties with Taiwan" - a partnership China views as a direct threat to its influence in the Horn of Africa.

a5290.speaker: China
a5290.speech: has denounced the partnership [between Somaliland and Taiwan] as a violation of its sovereignty and vowed to counter it.

a5290.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a5290.speech: recent remarks suggesting Washington was "looking into the Somaliland proposal" for recognition.

a5290.speaker: Analysts
a5290.speech: warn that Hodan's political ties and access to sensitive Somali security and diplomatic files could give Beijing unparalleled insight into Western intelligence cooperation in the Horn of Africa - a strategic prize for China's regional ambitions.

a5336.speaker: King Mohammed VI, President of the Al-Quds Committee
a5336.speech: Issued His High Instructions for the dispatch of emergency humanitarian and medical aid for the brotherly Palestinian people, in particular the people of the Gaza Strip.

a5336.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad of Morocco (press statement)
a5336.speech: Indicated on Wednesday that the King had ordered the dispatch of the aid, which has a total volume of nearly 180 tonnes and consists of basic foodstuffs, milk and products specially intended for children, as well as medicines and surgical equipment for the most vulnerable populations, plus blankets, suitable tents and other equipment; the aid will travel by a specially arranged route allowing rapid and direct delivery to the Palestinian beneficiaries. The statement concludes that this humanitarian aid falls within the framework of the concrete solidarity that constantly animates the Kingdom of Morocco, as well as of the unwavering commitment of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, President of the Al-Quds Committee, to the cause of Palestine and its brotherly people.

a5548.speaker: The Associated Press
a5548.speech: Declared President-elect Donald Trump the winner in Arizona on Saturday night after vote updates in Maricopa and other counties added to his overall lead, putting the state out of reach for Vice President Kamala Harris.

a5573.speaker: Mohammed Mwenga, Senior Social Behavior Change Advisor, USAID Afya Yangu Southern
a5573.speech: Said that it was an honour due hard work and determination which the project has been doing in improving health, well-being and protection of orphans, vulnerable children and youth in communities with high HIV burden.

a5573.speaker: Jessica Greene, PEPFAR Country Coordinator
a5573.speech: Said PEPFAR together with Tanzania Health Summit decided to come together and join efforts to celebrate heroes in the fight against HIV/AIDs ; 'These awards aim at recognizing excellence by acknowledging and celebrating organizations, Groups or Individuals who demonstrate outstanding contributions to the fight against HIV/AIDs, through effective and innovative programmatic strategies and interventions that have successfully reached or improved outcomes among youth, men, children and key vulnerable populations'.

a5581.speaker: Nanleeb Konlan, US-based businessman and founder of the Yennutona Foundation
a5581.speech: Presenting the items to the beneficiaries, said the gesture formed part of his annual support to the residents, particularly the vulnerable, in areas severely affected by the protracted conflicts and perennial drought ; “This lean season comes with serious food shortages. I believe this support will provide immediate relief and also help families refocus on other important areas of their lives, such as education, health, and work” ; stressed that the financial support given to some of the women would help boost their businesses, to enable them to support the upkeep of their homes, stating that “when women are economically empowered, the whole community thrives.”

a5581.speaker: Nanleeb Konlan, US-based businessman and founder of the Yennutona Foundation
a5581.speech: Said he had been able to use his influence to unite the people, lamenting that the conflict had caused havoc in the area for the past years, and said conflicts and peace were mutually exclusive; hence, the need for them to chart a new path for sustained peace to help rebuild the affected communities.

a5581.speaker: Beneficiaries of the foundation’s support
a5581.speech: Expressed their gratitude to the foundation for the support and said it would go a long way to improve their standard of living.

a5581.speaker: Laadi Mahamadu, beneficiary
a5581.speech: Emphasised how the items, especially the financial assistance, would help them reinvest in their petty trading and farming activities.

a5612.speaker: National Statistical Office (NSO) data / February 2025 Consumer Price Index (CPI)
a5612.speech: published NSO data shows Malawi’s year-on-year headline inflation rate for March 2025 declined by 0.2 percentage points to 30.5 percent, a marginal decline from the 30.7 percent recorded in February 2025; the CPI reads in part: “Food inflation now stands at 37.7 percent from 38.5 percent observed in February 2025 while non-food inflation is at 19.2 percent from 18.5 percent over the same period.”

a5612.speaker: John Kapito, Consumers Association of Malawi executive director
a5612.speech: said easing of maize prices will provide relief to consumers as it will have an impact on prices of goods and services: “Consumers will experiences huge relief in the cost of living, however, this is a short term relief.”

a5612.speaker: Nico Asset Managers Limited (February Monthly Economic Report)
a5612.speech: warned that inflationary headwinds will continue to linger, arising from fiscal slippages, which trigger money-supply growth and drive inflation, local currency weakness, increases in electricity tariffs and higher government expenditure due to the forthcoming September 16 General Elections.

a5612.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi and Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs
a5612.speech: expect inflation, which averaged 32.3 percent in 2024, to drop this year due to improved agricultural output.

a5703.speaker: Malian experts, notably economist Modibo Mao Makalou and former Trade Minister Harouna Niang
a5703.speech: addressed, during the panels, the challenges and opportunities of strengthened cooperation between the two countries, with discussions centred on key sectors such as energy, agriculture and import-export.

a5703.speaker: Mamadou Bah, President of the Perspective Sahélienne Association
a5703.speech: declared: "This day marks a historic moment for our association and for all those who believed in it, in the importance of strengthening economic ties between Mali and the Russian Federation" ; according to Mamadou Bah, Mali and Russia share a long history of diplomatic relations and cooperation: "Today, in a world context undergoing profound change, it is more necessary than ever to strengthen these ties in order to face the economic, security and environmental challenges affecting our respective regions," he stressed, adding that this forum constitutes a "unique opportunity to stimulate investment, promote trade and develop technological partnerships."

a5703.speaker: Ivan Ilinski, Press Attaché at the Russian Embassy in Bamako
a5703.speech: "This meeting is an opportunity to open new horizons for our cooperation. We are convinced that our partnership will continue to strengthen, thus contributing to the economic development of our countries."

a5703.speaker: Boubacar Tandia, First Vice-President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry
a5703.speech: For him, this forum is being held at a time when we are witnessing a significant strengthening of trade and economic relations between Mali and the Russian Federation.

a5826.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a5826.speech: Delivering the welcome address and overview of the retreat, painted a vivid picture of both the ambition and the challenges facing the Boakai administration’s national agenda ; "On January 15, 2025, we gathered in the beautiful city of Buchanan, Grand Bassa County, where His Excellency President Joseph Nyuma Boakai formally launched the Arrest Agenda and the 15 County Development Agendas," Ngafuan recalled. "This agenda encapsulates the ambitions of the Liberian people for development."

a5826.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a5826.speech: Disclosed that just weeks after the launch, Liberia’s development momentum was hit by a major setback: the unexpected withdrawal of support from one of its biggest donors ; "Nearly all projects supported by USAID, our second-largest donor, have been cancelled, except for two," he revealed. "The total cost of the cancelled projects could be upwards of $300 million, which has brought a level of unpredictability to our planning." ; acknowledged that the entire landscape of official development assistance is shifting, with many partners "backpedaling" due to internal financial pressures.

a5826.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a5826.speech: "The cost of implementing the Arrest Agenda is estimated at $8.38 billion, covering more than 370 critical interventions across all sectors," he said ; "From infrastructure to water, we are moving with speed, vim, and vigor." He cited specific goals such as reducing multidimensional poverty from 45% to 36% and increasing GDP per capita from $850 to $1,050 by 2029.

a5826.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a5826.speech: Emphasized that the government is proactively responding to the global shift by enhancing domestic resource mobilization and minimizing waste ; "We are rationalizing expenditure, reducing leakages and abuse, and digitizing processes to increase efficiency," he said.

a5826.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a5826.speech: Highlighted Liberia’s renewed focus on regional integration as a strategic path toward economic resilience ; "Whether it’s through ECOWAS, the African Union, or other mechanisms, we’re taking regional cooperation more seriously than ever before," he noted. "We’ve realized we’re less integrated with our neighbors than with countries outside the continent."

a5826.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a5826.speech: Called on development partners to engage in "frank conversations" and provide innovative solutions to help Liberia stay on course with its development vision ; "We have not come here in retreat, but to plan. We don’t have all the answers, but we know that together, we can generate ideas that will sustain the momentum of the Arrest Agenda," he said ; "We are going to take notes," Ngafuan concluded. "There may be a need to readjust, downgrade, or upgrade some areas. But one thing is certain, the Arrest Agenda will not sit on the shelf. We are serious about implementation."

a5826.speaker: Christine N. Umutoni, United Nations Resident Coordinator to Liberia
a5826.speech: Praised the government for its leadership in launching the AAID and acknowledged the shifting financial terrain globally ; "This retreat is an opportunity to engage in deep dialogue on how to strengthen partnerships," she said. "We must align our efforts to support Liberia’s national plan directly—through program budgeting, private sector engagement, civil society, and international partners."

a5826.speaker: Christine N. Umutoni, United Nations Resident Coordinator to Liberia
a5826.speech: Pointed to the importance of innovative financing and unlocking domestic potential, including through the private sector and Liberians in the diaspora ; "The private sector is not merely a participant in development; it is a catalyst for innovation, growth, and job creation," she stressed ; "Our diaspora carries invaluable knowledge and financial resources that can help shape Liberia’s future."

a5826.speaker: Christine N. Umutoni, United Nations Resident Coordinator to Liberia
a5826.speech: Praised the government’s willingness to embrace dynamic and adaptive strategies ; "The challenges we face are complex and multifaceted; our responses must be equally dynamic. We must be willing to adapt, innovate, and explore alternative financing mechanisms," Umutoni said.

a5916.speaker: Org Strauss, Bulls team doctor
a5916.speech: Stated earlier in the week that the openside flank Deon Stegmann would be out for between five to 10 days with a sprained ankle.

a5916.speaker: Information from Wellington (unattributed source)
a5916.speech: Suggests the Southern Kings will face a Hurricanes side strengthened by the return of fullback André Taylor, flank Ardie Savea, hooker Dane Coles and prop Jeffery Toomaga-Allen.

a5965.speaker: Ugandan and Kenyan ministers of trade (joint resolution/communique)
a5965.speech: Signed a joint resolution aimed at reducing trade barriers between the two states. The communique focuses on easing congestion at the common border to ensure that goods from both nations are cleared within two hours.

a6003.speaker: Mthuli Ncube, Finance Minister (no comment)
a6003.speech: The ex-African Development Bank chief economist and vice president was not reachable for comment this week.

a6035.speaker: Witnesses at Kakuma camp (anonymous)
a6035.speech: Said at least four people were wounded when Kenyan police opened fire on refugees demonstrating against severe shortages of food and water.

a6035.speaker: Mama Kayembe, Congolese refugee at Kakuma camp
a6035.speech: "Since Donald Trump came back to the head of the United States, Kenyans have placed all the blame on him. Workers are not paid and it's Trump's fault. No medicines at the hospital – it's Trump; now we have to pay school fees and it's Trump; everything is Trump. We have had enough of Trump. If Trump can hear us, we are humiliated here because of him. So let him change so that we stop being humiliated."

a6035.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and World Food Programme (WFP)
a6035.speech: Had previously warned that financial constraints could force them to reduce their operations.

a6326.speaker: Amara M. Konneh, Gbarpolu County Senator and Senate Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
a6326.speech: “We're thrilled about the news regarding the yellow machines! It is refreshing to hear that President Boakai has dramatically slashed costs, saving our country millions that would have otherwise lined personal pockets. We hear the new price is USD 22 million, a jaw-dropping three times less than before, a whopping USD 57 million savings! We hope he addresses procurement and public financial management (PFM) issues, as our country deserves quality roads free from corruption and politicization. We'll support him once the new scheme aligns with our laws! Thank you to the President for listening and delegating this task to Vice President Koung, who has done a fantastic job. There should be consequences for those who inflated the original costs and bypassed our PPCC and PFM Laws, scandalizing a good vision.” ; He also called for punitive actions to be taken against those who inflated the price of the yellow machines.

a6326.speaker: Government of Liberia (official announcement)
a6326.speech: Recently announced that it had renegotiated the price and terms of payment of 285 yellow machines, thus saving over $22 million, and that it had achieved favorable terms in renegotiating the purchase and shipment of the much anticipated 285 pieces of earth moving equipment.

a6326.speaker: Jerolinmek Piah, Liberian Information Minister and government spokesman
a6326.speech: According to Information Minister Piah, the committee set up by President Boakai and headed by Vice President Jeremiah Koung accessed possibilities of procuring the yellow machines considering price tag, shipment, and distribution across the 15 counties, and submitted a report to President Boakai. ; Said the first batch of payment is in the current budget 2025, and the suppliers will release the full quantity of the equipment after the first payment, adding that the government will complete the financial obligations over the next two years.

a6326.speaker: Report of the presidential committee headed by Vice President Jeremiah Koung
a6326.speech: The report assured citizens that the earth moving equipment will be brought in the same quantity (285 pcs) with significant reduction in the initial price. In the renegotiation, suppliers agreed to sell the machine at a total cost of US$22M. The payment, according to the report, will be consistent with the national budget, and the full amount completed within three years beginning 2025.

a6328.speaker: World Bank 2025 report on the assessment of policies and institutions in Africa (CPIA)
a6328.speech: One of the key lessons of the report is that, while more than half of sub-Saharan African countries face a high risk of debt distress or are already in debt distress, Benin stands out for the proactive management of its debt. ; According to the report, Benin ranks first with a score of 4.5 on debt policy and management, alongside Cote d'Ivoire and ahead of all other countries.

a6328.speaker: World Bank
a6328.speech: The World Bank is sounding the alarm: 53% of sub-Saharan African countries are now classified as at high risk of debt distress or already in distress, against only 25% in 2012, a figure that had reached 61% at the height of the crisis in 2021.

a6328.speaker: World Bank report
